title: Playgrounds
text: Playgrounds Learn Codly by changing a working example. Each page combines editable Typst source with controls for common options; Copy code captures your edits and the current control values, ready to paste into a document. Playground Try Layout and excerpts Fit long lines, compare themes, select source ranges, and add a review gutter. Annotations and references Highlight characters, attach explanations, and link to code from prose. Diffs and mixed languages Style a patch, tune its gutters, and highlight Python inside a shell script. See the API reference for complete field definitions, or queries and show rules for custom components.

title: Layout and excerpts
text: Layout and excerpts Tune a code block for the space around it, then select parts of a larger file without losing their source coordinates. Fit long lines Reduce the width to compare ordinary wrapping with smart indentation; the wrap marker appears on continuation lines when smart indentation is enabled. Row inset adds space around each line; block padding adds space around the whole block. Moving numbers outside places them beside the code border. - type: select name: layout-theme label: Theme default: '"github-light"' options: - label: GitHub Light value: '"github-light"' - label: Dark value: '"dark"' - label: Clean value: '"clean"' - type: slider name: layout-width label: Block width default: '100%' min: 55 max: 100 step: 5 unit: '%' - type: slider name: layout-size label: Code size default: '9pt' min: 7 max: 12 step: 1 unit: pt - type: slider name: layout-radius label: Corner radius default: '4pt' min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 unit: pt - type: slider name: layout-inset label: Row inset default: '3pt' min: 2 max: 8 step: 1 unit: pt - type: slider name: layout-padding label: Block padding default: '0pt' min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 unit: pt - type: switch name: layout-numbers label: Show line numbers default: true - type: switch name: layout-outside label: Numbers outside the block default: false - type: switch name: layout-smart-indent label: Smart indentation default: true - type: switch name: layout-wrap-marker label: Show wrap marker default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme(layout-theme, block: (text: (size: layout-size))) #show: codly.line-set_(inset: layout-inset) #show: codly.number-set_( placement: if layout-outside { "outside" } else { "inside" }, ) #codly.new( ```py def send_digest(address, updates): if updates: subject = "Your weekly project updates are ready to read" send_email(address, subject=subject, body=format_updates(updates)) return {"recipient": address, "delivered": bool(updates)} ```, file: "digest.py", width: layout-width, radius: layout-radius, padding: layout-padding, number-enabled: layout-numbers, smart-indent: layout-smart-indent, wrap-marker: if layout-wrap-marker { [↪] } else { none }, ) See codly.new for block fields and codly.theme for styling individual components. Show an excerpt with a review gutter The review marks belong to source lines 2, 4, and 7; they stay attached when the excerpt or numbering offset changes. - type: select name: excerpt-ranges label: Source selection default: none options: - label: Whole file value: none - label: Function body (2–7) value: '((2, 7),)' - label: Two excerpts (2–4 and 7–8) value: '((2, 4), (7, 8))' - type: slider name: excerpt-offset label: Numbering offset default: '0' min: 0 max: 100 step: 10 - type: switch name: excerpt-numbers label: Show line numbers default: true - type: switch name: excerpt-review label: Show review gutter default: true - type: slider name: excerpt-gutter-width label: Review gutter width default: '18pt' min: 12 max: 30 step: 2 unit: pt - type: switch name: excerpt-smart-skip label: Show omitted-line markers default: true - type: select name: excerpt-fills label: Row backgrounds default: '(rgb("f6f8fa"), white)' options: - label: Alternating value: '(rgb("f6f8fa"), white)' - label: Solid value: 'rgb("f6f8fa")' - label: No fill value: none - type: switch name: excerpt-guides label: Show indentation guides default: true - type: select name: excerpt-guide-width label: Spaces per guide level default: '4' options: - label: Infer from source value: auto - label: Two spaces value: '2' - label: Four spaces value: '4' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme("github-light", block: (text: (size: 9pt))) #show: codly.line-set_(fill: excerpt-fills) #codly.new( ```py def visible_names(records): names = [] for record in records: if record["active"]: name = record["name"].strip() names.append(name) return sorted(names) print(visible_names(records)) ```, file: "names.py", ranges: excerpt-ranges, offset: excerpt-offset, number-enabled: excerpt-numbers, smart-skip: excerpt-smart-skip, indent-guides: if excerpt-guides { (width: excerpt-guide-width) } else { false }, gutters: if excerpt-review { (auto, codly.gutter-column( values: (none, "?", none, "!", none, none, "✓", none), width: excerpt-gutter-width, align: center, text: (fill: rgb("8250df")), )) } else { auto }, ) [!NOTE] Source lines and displayed numbers differ. ranges and gutter arrays use original source lines. offset changes displayed numbers; it does not move the selected lines or review marks. See codly.range, codly.smart-skip, and codly.gutter-column for the selection and gutter rules. Continue with annotations and references to attach explanations to those lines.

title: Annotations and references
text: Annotations and references Mark expressions, group lines, attach notes, and link to all of them from prose. Highlights, annotations, and references References follow displayed numbering: change the offset and the highlight reference moves with it, while the annotation stays attached to the same source lines. - type: select name: highlight-palette label: Highlight palette default: '(blue, purple)' options: - label: Blue and purple value: '(blue, purple)' - label: Orange and red value: '(orange, red)' - label: Green and aqua value: '(green, aqua)' - type: slider name: highlight-start label: First character (zero-based) default: 9 min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 - type: slider name: highlight-length label: Highlight length default: 7 min: 1 max: 9 step: 1 - type: slider name: line-offset label: Displayed line offset default: 0 min: 0 max: 30 step: 1 - type: switch name: annotation-enabled label: Show the annotation default: true - type: slider name: annotation-end label: Last annotated source line default: 3 min: 2 max: 4 step: 1 - type: slider name: highlight-radius label: Highlight corner radius default: 3pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 8 step: 1 - type: select name: reference-mode label: Reference suffix default: '"line"' options: - label: Displayed line number value: '"line"' - label: Highlight tag or annotation text value: '"item"' - type: select name: highlight-tag label: Highlight tag default: '"step"' options: - label: step value: '"step"' - label: compute value: '"compute"' - label: result value: '"result"' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.highlight-set_(color: highlight-palette, radius: highlight-radius) #show: codly.ref-set_(by: reference-mode, sep: " · ") #figure(caption: [A processing pipeline])[ #codly.new( ```py data = load() result = compute(data) validate(result) return result ```, offset: line-offset, highlights: ( (line: 2 + line-offset, start: highlight-start, end: highlight-start + highlight-length, tag: highlight-tag, label: <selected-span>), (line: 4 + line-offset, start: 7, end: 13), ), annotations: if annotation-enabled { ((start: 2, end: annotation-end, content: [Processing], label: <processing>),) } else { () }, ) ]<analysis-code> The selected span is @selected-span. #if annotation-enabled [The annotated range is @processing.] The computation starts at #ref(label("analysis-code:" + str(2 + line-offset))). Highlight line values use displayed line numbers; their start and exclusive end count characters from zero. Annotation ranges use source line numbers, starting at one with an inclusive end. The labelled enclosing figure supplies the reference target automatically. Item references use a highlight's tag or an annotation's content. See highlight bounds, annotation ranges, and reference formatting. Pointed bubbles and plain callouts Two pointers on one line show how bubbles share a row or move into separate lanes as their preferred width and gap change. - type: select name: bubble-placement label: Bubble placement default: '"below"' options: - label: Below the source line value: '"below"' - label: Above the source line value: '"above"' - type: slider name: pointer-position label: First pointer character default: 13 min: 0 max: 25 step: 1 - type: select name: pointer-alignment label: Bubble alignment around pointer default: '"center"' options: - label: Start value: '"start"' - label: Center value: '"center"' - label: End value: '"end"' - type: slider name: bubble-width label: Preferred bubble width default: 100pt unit: pt min: 55 max: 145 step: 5 - type: slider name: bubble-gap label: Gap between bubbles default: 5pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 - type: select name: bubble-style label: Bubble paint default: '(fill: aqua.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + teal)' options: - label: Aqua with teal outline value: '(fill: aqua.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + teal)' - label: Yellow with orange outline value: '(fill: yellow.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + orange)' - label: White with gray outline value: '(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + gray)' - type: slider name: bubble-radius label: Bubble corner radius default: 4pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 10 step: 1 - type: switch name: source-indent label: Follow source indentation default: true - type: switch name: plain-callout-enabled label: Show the plain callout default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.bubble-set_( fill: bubble-style.fill, stroke: bubble-style.stroke, width: bubble-width, gap: bubble-gap, radius: bubble-radius, pointer-align: pointer-alignment, ) #show: codly.callout-set_(source-indent: source-indent) #codly.new( ```py def invoice(subtotal, tax): total = subtotal + tax return total print(invoice(80, 16)) ```, callouts: ( (line: 2, pointer: pointer-position, placement: bubble-placement, body: [The base amount before tax.]), (line: 2, pointer: 24, placement: bubble-placement, body: [Tax is added once.]), ) + if plain-callout-enabled { ((line: 3, body: [The computed total is returned.]),) } else { () }, ) Callout line values use source lines, unaffected by numbering offsets. A pointer counts source characters from one, with 0 anchoring the start; pointer: none makes a plain callout. Only plain callouts follow source-indent. Bubble width is a preference: Codly keeps each bubble within the available row and wraps its text. See callout configuration and bubble styles. To style selected elements with show rules, continue with queries and show rules.

title: Diffs and mixed languages
text: Diffs and mixed languages Highlight changes in a patch, and embedded code inside another language. Review a Python change This patch replaces a positional result with named fields. Old and new code get independent syntax passes, so removed delimiters or multiline strings do not disturb the highlighting of added code. The custom gutter shows patch-row coordinates and replaces the automatic old/new/marker columns. - type: switch name: patch-enabled label: Process the patch default: true - type: switch name: patch-numbers label: Old and new numbers default: true - type: switch name: patch-markers label: Added and removed markers default: true - type: select name: patch-colors label: Change colors default: '(added: rgb("dafbe1"), removed: rgb("ffebe9"), meta: rgb("ddf4ff"))' options: - label: Green and red value: '(added: rgb("dafbe1"), removed: rgb("ffebe9"), meta: rgb("ddf4ff"))' - label: Blue and orange value: '(added: rgb("dbeafe"), removed: rgb("ffedd5"), meta: rgb("f1f5f9"))' - label: No background value: '(added: none, removed: none, meta: none)' - type: slider name: patch-old-offset label: Old number offset default: '0' min: 0 max: 100 step: 10 - type: slider name: patch-new-offset label: New number offset default: '0' min: 0 max: 100 step: 10 - type: switch name: patch-custom-gutter label: Custom patch-row gutter default: false - type: switch name: patch-rainbow label: Color nested delimiters default: true - type: slider name: patch-width label: Block width default: '100%' min: 55 max: 100 step: 5 unit: '%' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```diff-py @@ -20,3 +20,6 @@ def summarize(values): - totals = [sum(values), len(values)] - return totals + totals = { + "sum": sum(values), + "count": len(values), + } + return totals ```, diff: if patch-enabled { ( numbers: patch-numbers, markers: patch-markers, added-fill: patch-colors.added, removed-fill: patch-colors.removed, meta-fill: patch-colors.meta, old-offset: patch-old-offset, new-offset: patch-new-offset, ) } else { false }, gutters: if patch-custom-gutter { (codly.gutter-column( values: row => if row.source-line != none { "R" + str(row.source-line) }, align: right, text: (fill: gray), ),) } else { auto }, rainbow: patch-rainbow, width: patch-width, ) Both diff-py and diff,py are valid Codly language tags. The hyphenated fence also works in Typst 0.15; on versions without comma support in fences, use raw(source, block: true, lang: "diff,py"). See codly.diff for patch coordinates and codly.gutter-column for custom columns. Highlight Python inside a shell script The shell launches Python through a heredoc, so lines 3–10 need Python highlighting inside a shell block. Without the sublanguage, the shell grammar treats that region as a string. Each sublanguage has its own delimiter stack. Rainbow coloring skips delimiters in strings and comments, and indentation guides follow leading spaces. - type: switch name: embedded-enabled label: Highlight embedded code default: true - type: select name: embedded-language label: Embedded language default: '"py"' options: - label: Python value: '"py"' - label: Plain text value: '"text"' - type: switch name: syntax-rainbow label: Color nested delimiters default: true - type: select name: syntax-palette label: Delimiter and guide palette default: '(rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a"))' options: - label: Red, blue, green value: '(rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a"))' - label: Purple, teal, orange value: '(rgb("7c3aed"), rgb("0f766e"), rgb("c2410c"))' - label: One blue value: '(rgb("005cc5"),)' - type: slider name: syntax-depth-offset label: Starting palette index default: '0' min: 0 max: 4 step: 1 - type: switch name: syntax-guides label: Show indentation guides default: true - type: select name: syntax-indent-width label: Spaces per guide level default: '4' options: - label: Infer from source value: auto - label: Two spaces value: '2' - label: Four spaces value: '4' - type: switch name: syntax-numbers label: Show line numbers default: true - type: slider name: syntax-width label: Block width default: '100%' min: 55 max: 100 step: 5 unit: '%' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash python3 - <<'PY' def summarize(values): stats = { "sum": sum(values), "count": len(values), } return {"stats": stats, "items": list(values)} print(summarize([2, 4, 8])) PY echo "Report ready" ```, sublangs: if embedded-enabled { (codly.sublang(start: 3, end: 10, lang: embedded-language),) } else { () }, rainbow: ( enabled: syntax-rainbow, palette: syntax-palette, depth-offset: syntax-depth-offset, ), indent-guides: ( enabled: syntax-guides, width: syntax-indent-width, ), number-enabled: syntax-numbers, width: syntax-width, ) Sublanguage ranges count original source lines, starting at 1. If you insert lines above the Python section, update start and end in the editor. See codly.sublang, codly.rainbow, and codly.indent-guides for the individual options, or Internals for the rendering pipeline.

title: Migrating from 1.3.0 / 1.3.1
text: Migrating from 1.3.0 and 1.3.1 to 2.0 Version 2 replaces state-changing configuration calls with explicit code elements and scoped show rules. Most data structures carry over unchanged; styling moves to the component that owns it. This guide covers both 1.3.0 and 1.3.1, whose configuration APIs are identical. Where 1.3.1 behavior differs — nested highlights, local highlight overrides, icon spacing, reference and grid fixes — the relevant section says so. Each section shows the old code, its replacement, and an editable 2.0 example. The 1.3 snippets are for comparison only; widget controls and source edits apply to the new example, and Copy code captures both. If your document uses… Start here codly-init, codly(...), or local(...) Initialization and scoped settings Enable/disable helpers Conversion boundaries inset, stroke, fill, or zebra-fill Geometry and typography and row fills languages, lang-*, or lang-format Language definitions and formatters Headers, footers, or filename presentation Headers and footers and filenames Ranges, skips, or continued numbering Ranges, explicit skips, and offsets Number formatting or hidden numbers Number styling and visibility Highlights or annotations Whole-line highlights, character spans, and annotations References or internal queries References and custom rules and queries ::: collapse Update imports and initialize automatic conversion {#initialization} In 1.3, codly-init installed the raw-block show rules and figure handling. The codly function then changed configuration; it did not take a code block as its positional body. Before — 1.3.0 or 1.3.1: #import "@preview/codly:1.3.1": * #show: codly-init #codly(number-format: numbering.with("1.")) After — 2.0: import the namespace, set defaults with show rules, and register codly.new as the raw-block converter. codly.new(body, ..fields) constructs a block; the exported codly.codly is an alias of this constructor, not the old configuration function. - type: switch name: setup-numbers label: Show line numbers default: true - type: select name: setup-numbering label: Number format default: '"1."' options: - label: Plain value: '"1"' - label: With a dot value: '"1."' - label: In parentheses value: '"(1)"' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.set_(number-enabled: setup-numbers) #show: codly.number-set_(numbering: setup-numbering) #show raw.where(block: true): codly.new ```py def greet(name): return f"Hello, {name}!" print(greet("reader")) ``` The selector only converts block raw content; inline raw keeps Typst's ordinary rendering. If you build every listing with an explicit #codly.new(...), omit the converter rule entirely. Codly 2.0 requires Typst 0.15 or newer. These examples import @preview/codly:2.0.0; when working from a checkout, import "codly.typ" or a locally installed "@local/codly:2.0.0" instead. See codly.new for accepted bodies and fields. ::: ::: collapse Replace configuration state with scoped defaults and explicit blocks {#scoped-settings} In 1.3, #codly(...) mutated state for the raw blocks that followed. local(...) applied temporary overrides, with nested: true to merge an enclosing local configuration. Block-specific settings — ranges, offsets, skips, highlights, annotations, headers, footers — were reset after each block. Before: #import "@preview/codly:1.3.1": * #show: codly-init #codly(radius: 2pt) #local(radius: 8pt, nested: true)[ ```py special = True ``` ] ```py ordinary = True ``` After: place #show: codly.set_(...) in the scope whose blocks should inherit it. Component setters work the same way. An explicit argument on codly.new overrides that block's scoped default. Nested scopes inherit outer rules without a nested flag. - type: slider name: scope-outer-radius label: Outer corner radius default: 2pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 - type: slider name: scope-inner-radius label: Inner corner radius default: 8pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 - type: slider name: scope-padding label: First block padding default: 3pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 8 step: 1 - type: switch name: scope-first-numbers label: First block numbers default: false #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme("github-light") #show: codly.set_(radius: scope-outer-radius) #{ show: codly.set_(radius: scope-inner-radius) codly.new( ```py special = True ```, padding: scope-padding, number-enabled: scope-first-numbers, ) } #codly.new( ```py ordinary = True ```, ) Scoped defaults apply to every matching element that follows in the scope; they are not consumed by the next block. Pass one-off data (ranges, skips, highlights, annotations) directly to codly.new, and keep shared defaults in show rules. Reusing a labelled highlight across blocks creates duplicate labels. There is no codly-reset equivalent: end the scope to restore the enclosing configuration. To reset presentation inside a scope, apply a theme or explicit component defaults — but note that a theme does not clear block data such as ranges or annotations. #set codly.new(...) is not an Elembic set rule. Use #show: codly.set_(...) for block defaults and the component setters (codly.line-set_, codly.lang-set_, …) for component fields. ::: ::: collapse Keep existing block behavior options {#retained-block-options} Several familiar fields stay on the block. Move them from #codly(...) or local(...) to the corresponding codly.new(..., field: value) call; use codly.set_ only when the value should apply throughout a scope. Field retained from 1.3 What it controls aliases Maps an authored language key to a syntax-highlighting language. Language badge definitions still belong to codly.lang. smart-indent Keeps continuation lines aligned with source indentation. skip-last-empty Omits the final empty source line when enabled. breakable Allows the code block to split across pages. Header/footer repetition requires a breakable block. If a 1.3 field accepted a zero-argument function as a lazy value, call it yourself and pass the result; 2.0 fields expect concrete values. The example also uses two new 2.0 controls, width and wrap-marker; the marker only appears when smart indentation is enabled. - type: switch name: retained-alias label: Resolve the custom Python alias default: true - type: switch name: retained-smart-indent label: Smart indentation default: true - type: switch name: retained-skip-empty label: Omit the final empty line default: true - type: slider name: retained-width label: Block width default: 100% unit: '%' min: 55 max: 100 step: 5 - type: switch name: retained-wrap-marker label: Show wrap markers default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme("github-light", block: (text: (size: 9pt))) #show: codly.lang-set_(languages: (example-python: "Python")) #codly.new( ```example-python def notify(address, updates): if updates: send_email(address, subject="Your project updates", body=format_updates(updates)) ```, aliases: if retained-alias { (example-python: "py") } else { (:) }, smart-indent: retained-smart-indent, skip-last-empty: retained-skip-empty, width: retained-width, wrap-marker: if retained-wrap-marker { [↪] } else { none }, ) When checking a migrated wrapped listing, compare indentation as well as row counts: a wrapped continuation is still part of its source line. The headers and footers example uses a finite page height if you need to check pagination. ::: ::: collapse Port enable and disable helpers to conversion boundaries {#enable-and-disable} The 1.3 helpers codly-enable, codly-disable, no-codly, and yes-codly controlled the state checked by codly-init. The 2.0 constructor has no enabled field: calling it means that you want a Codly block. Before: #import "@preview/codly:1.3.1": * #show: codly-init #codly-disable() ```text Ordinary raw text ``` #codly-enable() ```py print("formatted") ``` After: choose where conversion happens. For occasional listings, leave raw blocks alone and call codly.new explicitly. For automatic conversion, write one routing rule that returns the original raw element for excluded blocks — here, everything tagged text: - type: switch name: conversion-enabled label: Convert code blocks default: true - type: switch name: conversion-exclude-text label: Keep text blocks ordinary default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show raw.where(block: true): it => { if conversion-enabled and not ( conversion-exclude-text and it.lang == "text" ) { codly.new(it) } else { it } } ```py print("formatted") ``` ```text An ordinary text block ``` Adjust the predicate to your own exclusion policy, or place the converter inside a local scope so raw blocks outside it stay ordinary. [!IMPORTANT] Keep the bypass in the routing rule. A later show raw.where(block: true): it => it does not reliably undo an earlier converter — the element still passes through the older rule. Port no-codly wrappers by extending the converter's exclusion policy or by scoping the converter itself. [!TIP] Disable Codly with a label Tag a raw block with a label such as <native> and test it in the routing rule to opt individual blocks out (or in): #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show raw.where(block: true): it => { if "label" in it.fields() and it.label == <native> { it } else { codly.new(it) } } ```py print("native") ``` <native> ```py print("formatted") ``` ::: ::: collapse Typography, row spacing, and the code border {#migration-typography-and-spacing} Move presentation to its component; keep geometry on the block. Version 1 combined row inset, border, and outer radius in a single configuration call. Version 2 separates them: Version 1 Version 2 inset: ... #show: codly.line-set_(inset: ...) stroke: ... #show: codly.line-set_(stroke: ...) radius: ... codly.new(..., radius: ...), or scoped codly.set_ Native raw/text typography Native rules, or the text dictionary of a theme section Neither 1.3 release had a Codly-specific font option. Native text rules still apply; for Codly-only typography, use a theme's block.text dictionary, or number.text, lang.text, header.text, and footer.text for individual components. Place narrower rules after the theme so they take precedence. Version 1: #show raw: set text(font: "DejaVu Sans Mono", size: 9pt) #codly(inset: 4pt, stroke: 1pt + luma(180), radius: 6pt) The new padding field adds space at the block edges, independent of row inset — do not port inset to padding. Version 2 also adds leading, gutter, column-gutter, and row-gutter on the block; leading sets vertical row spacing, replacing the vertical components of the old inset. These are new controls, not renames. - type: select name: migration-code-font label: Code font default: '"DejaVu Sans Mono"' options: - label: DejaVu Sans Mono value: '"DejaVu Sans Mono"' - label: Noto Sans Mono value: '"Noto Sans Mono"' - type: slider name: migration-code-size label: Code size default: 9pt unit: pt min: 7 max: 12 step: 1 - type: slider name: migration-row-inset label: Row inset default: 4pt unit: pt min: 1 max: 8 step: 1 - type: slider name: migration-edge-padding label: Block edge padding default: 0pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 10 step: 1 - type: slider name: migration-block-radius label: Outer corner radius default: 6pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme( "thesis", block: (text: (font: migration-code-font, size: migration-code-size)), lang: (text: (font: "Source Sans 3", size: 9pt)), ) #show: codly.line-set_(inset: migration-row-inset, stroke: 1pt + luma(180)) #codly.new( ```py def greet(name): return f"Welcome back, {name}!" print(greet("Ada")) ```, radius: migration-block-radius, padding: migration-edge-padding, ) If a 1.3.0 document depended on document-wide grid or grid.cell rules leaking into Codly (1.3.1 already isolated its grid), re-check the layout; version 2 exposes the supported presentation changes as component fields instead. See codly.line, codly.new, and themes. ::: ::: collapse Background fills, zebra striping, and fill callbacks {#migration-row-fills} Replace the two old background settings with one row fill. zebra-fill is removed. codly.line accepts a single paint, none, a nonempty palette, or a callback. Version 1: #codly(fill: white, zebra-fill: luma(240)) Version 2's matching alternating configuration is: #show: codly.line-set_(fill: (luma(240), white)) The order matters: entry 0 paints displayed row 0, entry 1 paints row 1. An old zebra-fill: none becomes a scalar fill: <old fill>; an empty palette is invalid. fill: auto restores the default alternating pattern. Displayed rows are not source lines. Palette indexing counts generated skip rows, callout rows, and header/footer rows. Headers and footers have their own backgrounds but still advance the index, so a header shifts the stripe of the first code line. For striping by source-line parity, use the callback's source-line field instead. The callback receives one row dictionary: Field Meaning index Zero-based position among displayed rows, including generated rows. kind "code", "skip", or "callout" for callback rows. source-line One-based source line for code/callout rows; none for skips. number Displayed line number after offsets/skips; none for unnumbered/generated rows. Headers and footers never call this function. Whole-line highlights and enabled diff backgrounds take precedence over the row fill. Note the changed callback contract: 1.3 accepted zero-argument lazy values such as fill: () => color, but the 2.0 fill callback is a row formatter. Write fill: row => ..., or evaluate the old helper yourself (fill: helper()). To replace the brace entirely, use annotation-show_: read body, height, num, numbering, and the hidden label content with codly.e.fields(it), and keep that resolved label content in your replacement so references keep their anchor. - type: slider name: migration-annotation-start label: First source line default: '2' min: 1 max: 3 step: 1 - type: slider name: migration-annotation-end label: Last source line default: '4' min: 3 max: 4 step: 1 - type: switch name: migration-annotation-number label: Show the annotation number default: true - type: switch name: migration-annotation-rotate label: Rotate its text default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py def process(): load() compute() save() process() ```, annotations: (( start: migration-annotation-start, end: migration-annotation-end, content: if migration-annotation-rotate { rotate(-90deg, reflow: true)[body] } else { [body] }, numbering: if migration-annotation-number { numbering.with("(a)") } else { none }, ),), ) See annotation-config and annotation. ::: ::: collapse Keep native references and move their formatting rules {#migration-references} Your existing @block:2, @highlight-label, and @annotation-label references can stay. Keep a label on the enclosing figure; codly.new discovers it automatically, so you do not need to repeat it as block-label. Item labels still belong on their highlight or annotation configuration. // 1.3.0 / 1.3.1: #codly( reference-by: "item", reference-sep: " — ", reference-number-format: numbering.with("I"), ) // 2.0: #show: codly.ref-set_( by: "item", sep: " — ", numbering: numbering.with("I"), ) Line labels are built from the displayed integer, before the visual numbering pattern: a block with Roman numbering still uses @block:2, not @block:II. If an offset shows source line 2 as number 12, the label becomes @block:12 — keep references and highlight coordinates consistent with that mapping. by: "line" refers to highlights and annotations by displayed line; by: "item" uses a highlight's tag, which must exist. Annotation item references changed: they now use the annotation's content instead of its formatted number. If you relied on a suffix like (a), switch to displayed-line references or override the generated codly.annotation-ref: #show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => { let fields = codly.e.fields(it) [#ref(fields.block) — (a)] }) Hiding the annotation number does not hide its item content. For unnumbered source lines, use labels such as @block:l2p1: l2 is the preceding displayed number and p1 counts consecutive unnumbered lines after it. Numbered lines keep the normal @block:2 form. Each reference kind is now its own generated element — codly.line-ref, codly.highlight-ref, and codly.annotation-ref — with its own *-set_ and *-show_ wrappers; ref-set_ supplies the shared defaults. In a show callback, read the containing block label and the number/item fields with codly.e.fields(it), and return ref(fields.block) to keep the figure reference's normal formatting. - type: select name: migration-ref-mode label: Highlight and annotation references default: '"line"' options: - label: Displayed line number value: '"line"' - label: Item tag or content value: '"item"' - type: select name: migration-ref-separator label: Reference separator default: '" — "' options: - label: Dash value: '" — "' - label: Colon value: '":"' - label: Line wording value: '" line "' - type: select name: migration-ref-numbering label: Reference number format default: 'numbering.with("1")' options: - label: Decimal value: 'numbering.with("1")' - label: Roman value: 'numbering.with("I")' - label: Figure reference only value: none #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.ref-set_( by: migration-ref-mode, sep: migration-ref-separator, numbering: migration-ref-numbering, ) #figure(caption: [A migrated code block])[ #codly.new( ```py def process(): result = compute() return result ```, highlights: (( line: 2, start: 4, end: 10, tag: [value], label: <migration-value>, ),), annotations: (( start: 2, end: 3, content: [body], label: <migration-body>, ),), ) ]<migration-code> Line: @migration-code:2. \ Highlight: @migration-value. \ Annotation: @migration-body. See reference settings, line-ref, highlight-ref, and annotation-ref. ::: ::: collapse Port lazy settings, custom show rules, and queries {#custom-rules-and-queries} Many 1.3 settings accepted a zero-argument function as a lazy value, e.g. #codly(radius: () => chosen-radius). In 2.0, each field declares its accepted types: a radius takes a length, so pass chosen-radius directly. Genuine callbacks keep their documented contracts — a number formatter receives a number, a highlight paint transformer a resolved paint, a row-fill callback a row dictionary. Do not mechanically rewrite every old function-valued setting. To decorate or replace a generated element, install a *-show_ callback. It receives an Elembic element; read its resolved fields with codly.e.fields(it), always using Codly's own codly.e export so element identities match. The rule below decorates one number while keeping the normal renderer: - type: slider name: custom-number label: Decorated number default: 2 min: 1 max: 3 step: 1 - type: select name: custom-accent label: Decoration color default: purple options: - label: Purple value: purple - label: Red value: red - label: Teal value: teal - type: switch name: custom-bold label: Bold decoration default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.number-show_(it => { let fields = codly.e.fields(it) if fields.number == custom-number { text( fill: custom-accent, weight: if custom-bold { "bold" } else { "regular" }, it, ) } else { it } }) #codly.new( ```py data = load() result = compute(data) save(result) ```, ) #context { let blocks = codly.e.query(codly.new, before: here()) [Blocks before this paragraph: #blocks.len().] } Returning it (possibly wrapped) keeps the built-in renderer, including its formatting and anchors; returning fresh content replaces it. Constructing the same component inside its own show rule re-triggers the rule. Scripts that inspected state("codly-..."), internal figures, or nested .body.children relied on 1.3 implementation details and must be rewritten. Use codly.e.query for element instances, codly.e.fields for fields, codly.e.get for scoped defaults, and codly.info for a labelled block's source-line count and last displayed number. Query inside context, and never make an element's existence depend on a query that counts that same element. Native selectors such as codly.selector() work in show rules, but their default representation layers can match intermediate renderings, so they are not interchangeable with codly.e.query for counting instances. title: API reference
text: API reference Components render code blocks and their parts. Types describe configuration values and their accepted shorthand forms. Themes and helpers apply reusable styles and inspect block metadata. ⚙️ Queries and show rules explains how to inspect and customize elements. ⚙️ Internals follows a code block from source to layout and references. Imports Import the Codly package as a namespace: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly Components and styling [!TIP] Style components with show rules. Use #show: codly.number-set_(...) to set defaults in scope. The *-show_ helpers accept replacement content or a callback receiving the component, rather than a dictionary of field overrides. Codly uses Elembic custom elements and types; the exported codly.e gives you the same Elembic version without a separate import. codly.new creates a code block, and component helpers such as codly.number-set_ apply scoped defaults with #show: rather than native #set syntax. See the Elembic documentation for details. #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.number-set_(numbering: "1.") #show raw.where(block: true): codly.new ```py print(42) print(43) ``` Each component page documents its constructor and its *-set_ and *-show_ helpers. Configuration types do not render directly — Codly instantiates them internally — and most accept dictionaries or arrays in place of an explicit constructor call; each type page lists its accepted forms. Coordinates and defaults [!NOTE] Source coordinates Source-line ranges are one-indexed and inclusive. Character highlights use zero-indexed offsets with an exclusive end. Displayed line numbers can change with offsets and skipped lines. Callout pointers and explicit skip positions have their own conventions, documented on their type pages. Check a field's definition before using displayed numbers as configuration coordinates. auto and none have field-specific meanings. A default value does not always describe the final appearance: themes, scoped styling rules, and surrounding Typst text or raw settings can affect rendering. paint means a color, gradient, or tiling; array<T> an array of T values. [!WARNING] Signatures describe types. Signature blocks show the accepted argument types; they are not runnable Typst examples. Use the preview examples as a starting point for your code.

title: Components
text: Components Components render blocks, badges, rows, annotations, and references. Their pages also document the associated scoped styling helpers. codly.new codly.lang codly.file codly.header codly.footer codly.line codly.number codly.highlight codly.annotation codly.bubble codly.callout codly.ref codly.line-ref codly.highlight-ref codly.annotation-ref codly.sublang-block

title: new
text: codly.new Creates a formatted code block. codly.new is an alias of codly.codly; codly.set_, codly.show_, and codly.selector target the same element. Signature codly.new(body, ..fields) body is positional and required. It accepts source text, a path, or content containing raw blocks. Other fields are named. The setters accept named field values; show_ installs a scoped replacement callback, and selector creates a Typst selector for block instances. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | str | path | content Required, positional Raw content, literal source text, or a caller-resolved file path. file auto | none | str | path | content auto Filename badge content; auto uses an input path basename, and none hides the badge. lang auto | none | str auto Language for source text or path inputs; auto infers the file extension. lang-position auto | none | alignment auto Language badge placement. Top or bottom places it in a header or footer; left or right alone reserves space beside the first code row. auto uses ordinary placement; none hides the badge. file-position none | alignment top + left Filename badge placement. Top or bottom places it in a header or footer; left or right alone reserves space beside the first code row. none hides it. block-label auto | none | label auto Label used for block and item references. auto discovers the nearest enclosing figure's label; none disables generated references. alias none | str none Internal original language key identifying a block whose syntax alias has already been resolved. number-enabled none | bool true Whether to include the automatic line-number column. diff none | auto | diff auto Diff configuration or enablement flag. auto detects diff-<language> and diff,<language>; false or none disables processing. Diff code is highlighted independently for old and new sides. gutters auto | array<auto | gutter-column> auto Ordered gutter columns. auto includes the automatic number column when enabled; an empty array hides all gutters. Custom columns remain when number-enabled is false. offset int | label | auto 0 Displayed-number offset. An integer is added to source numbers; auto starts the first selected source line at one. A block or figure label continues after its last displayed number. range none | range none Inclusive one-based source-line range to display; none selects all lines. ranges none | array<range> none Inclusive one-based source-line ranges to display. Cannot be combined with range. smart-skip none | smart-skip false Whether to generate omission rows around selected ranges, or a configuration controlling leading, interior, and trailing omissions separately. aliases none | dictionary (:) Dictionary mapping displayed language keys to syntax-highlighting language keys. smart-indent none | bool true Whether wrapped continuations retain indentation from the normalized source text. wrap-marker none | content none Content displayed at each wrapped continuation when smart-indent is enabled. skip-last-empty none | bool true Whether to omit the final source line when it contains only whitespace. breakable none | bool true Whether the code block can span pages and columns. skips none | array<skip> none Explicit omission rows inserted before one-based source lines. Their lengths increase subsequent displayed numbers without removing supplied source lines. skip-line none | content | array<none | content> align(center)[ ... ] Omission-row content, or values indexed by explicit skip order. Further and smart skips reuse the final value; an empty array uses the default. skip-number none | content | array<none | content> [ ... ] Omission number-cell content, or values indexed by explicit skip order. Further and smart skips reuse the final value; an empty array uses the default. unnumbered none | array<unnumbered-line> () One-based source lines excluded from numbering, with optional number-cell content. Their references use the preceding displayed number and an ordinal suffix. annotations none | array<annotation-config> none Brace annotation configurations covering inclusive one-based source-line ranges in the rightmost grid column. callouts none | array<callout-config> none Content attached above or below one-based source lines. A pointer selects a source character and enables a bubble. Entry styling overrides codly.callout settings, which override codly.bubble defaults. highlighted none | array<highlighted-line> () Whole-row highlight configurations keyed by displayed line numbers, including offsets and skips. Explicit paints override the default highlight palette. highlights none | array<highlight-config> none Character highlight configurations keyed by displayed line numbers. Character bounds are zero-based with an exclusive end; omitted bounds select the complete line. header none | content none Content displayed in a header row; codly.header content preserves its explicit cell settings. footer none | content none Content displayed in a footer row; codly.footer content preserves its explicit cell settings. radius none | length 0.32em Corner radius of the containing code grid. padding length | dictionary 0pt Additional padding at block edges, separate from row inset and leading. Accepts a length or a Typst inset dictionary. leading none | length none Vertical padding of each code row, overriding the vertical line inset while retaining its horizontal component. gutter none | length none Default spacing between grid rows and columns. column-gutter none | length none Spacing between grid columns, overriding gutter horizontally. row-gutter none | length none Spacing between grid rows, overriding gutter vertically. sublangs none | array<sublang> none Syntax-highlighting languages assigned to inclusive one-based source-line ranges. rainbow none | rainbow none Optional syntax-aware delimiter coloring; true enables the default configuration. indent-guides none | indent-guides none Optional indentation guides; true enables the default configuration. width length | ratio | auto 100% Block width; auto fits the natural width up to the available width. Behavior [!TIP] Figure labels are discovered automatically. Label the enclosing figure once. Codly discovers that label automatically, so omit the block-label argument from codly.new. [!WARNING] Unlabeled inner figures stop discovery. A code block inside an unlabeled nested figure does not inherit an outer figure's label. Label the inner figure to enable references to its code. [!WARNING] Sublanguages cost performance. Each sublang block requires re-parsing and introspection; heavy use slows compilation. Fields are validated and cast by their declared types. Gutter arrays and functions cast to gutter-column; gutters: auto includes the ordinary number column when enabled, and custom columns remain when number-enabled is false. Custom gutters replace diff's automatic old/new/marker columns. Diff colors may be paints, none, auto (the ordinary row fill), or callbacks receiving a row with diff information. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff backgrounds. Ranges select source lines before display. Diff references count displayed patch rows; highlight and callout character positions count code characters without diff markers. Diff context uses new-side syntax, and each hunk or file is highlighted independently. #show: codly.set_(..fields) sets named field defaults in scope. #show: codly.show_(it => content) replaces matching blocks with the callback result; return it inside the result to retain the block. #show codly.selector(): it => content uses a native Typst selector. selector accepts outline, outer, and meta boolean options, all defaulting to false; these select Elembic representation layers rather than filtering fields. Example - type: select name: example-language label: Language default: '"python"' options: - label: Python value: '"python"' - label: Rust value: '"rust"' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #set raw(lang: example-language) #codly.new( ``` def greet(name): print(f'Hello, {name}!') ```, file: "greeting.py", offset: 10, ) Example: Automatic Code Blocks #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show raw.where(block: true): codly.new ```py def greet(name): print(f'Hello, {name}!') ```

title: lang
text: codly.lang Creates the language badge used by a Codly code block, with language definitions and badge styling. Signature // Define a language badge for a Codly code block. codly.lang( body: str, languages: dictionary | none = (:), default-color: paint | none = rgb("#283593"), inset: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em, outset: dictionary | none = (x: 0.32em, y: 0em), radius: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em, stroke: stroke | function | none = (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt, fill: paint | function | none = (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%), display-name: bool | none = true, display-icon: bool | none = true, align: alignment | none = right + horizon, ) // Equivalent set-rule for a language badge. codly.lang-set_(..args) // Override the show-rule for a language badge. codly.lang-show_(it, ..args) body is the required positional language key (for example, "py"). All other fields are named. codly.lang-set_(..args) sets defaults for language badges in its scope; codly.lang-show_(it => ...) installs a show rule that receives each badge element and returns replacement content. These helpers use the same field names as the element. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body str Required, positional Language key used to select a language definition. languages none | dictionary<language> (:) Dictionary mapping language keys to definitions. Missing keys display the original language key with default-color. default-color none | paint rgb("#283593") Badge color used when the language definition supplies no color. inset none | length | dictionary 0.32em Padding inside the language badge, as a length or a Typst inset dictionary. outset none | dictionary (x: 0.32em, y: 0em) Horizontal and vertical badge placement offsets, given by the x and y keys. radius none | length | dictionary 0.32em Corner radius of the language badge. stroke none | stroke | function (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt Badge border, or a callback receiving the resolved name, icon, and color. fill none | paint | function (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%) Badge background, or a callback receiving the resolved name, icon, and color. A scalar none falls back to the language color. display-name none | bool true Whether to display the language name. display-icon none | bool true Whether to display the language icon. align none | alignment right + horizon Alignment used for an ordinary inline language badge. Behavior [!TIP] Unknown language keys stay visible. If languages has no matching entry, the badge shows the raw language key and uses default-color. Add a definition when you want a display name or icon. The languages dictionary maps raw language tags to codly.language values. Its values also accept a string as shorthand for a displayed name, or a dictionary. A missing entry displays the raw key and uses default-color; a matching entry supplies its name, optional icon, and optional color. Language definitions can preserve extra fields. For a matching key, display-name, display-icon, fill, stroke, inset, and radius in that definition override the corresponding badge fields. The definition's color is used by fill and stroke callbacks through their lang dictionary; outset, align, and default-color are not per-language overrides. If both name and icon are hidden or unavailable, the badge renders no content. Setting fill or stroke to none removes that decoration. Example: Typical Usage - type: slider name: badge-radius label: Badge radius default: 4pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.lang-set_( radius: badge-radius, languages: ( py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("#3476a8"), icon: "🐍"), ), ) #codly.lang( "py", inset: 5pt, ) Example: Custom Renderer #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.lang-set_(languages: ( py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("#3476a8"), icon: "🐍"), )) #show: codly.lang-show_(it => { // Get the fields through elembic let fields = codly.e.fields(it) // Get the language definition let lang = fields.languages.at(fields.body, default: none) if lang == none { return none } // Make a custom badge box( fill: lang.color.lighten(80%), stroke: 1pt + lang.color, outset: 0pt, inset: 2pt, [ #lang.name - #lang.icon ], ) }) #codly.new(```py def main(): print("Hello, Python!") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```)

title: file
text: codly.file Creates the filename badge used beside a code block or in its header or footer. Signature // Create a filename badge codly.file( body: str | content, fill: paint | none = luma(240), stroke: stroke | none = 0.5pt + luma(160), inset: length | dictionary = (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em), radius: length | dictionary = 2pt, ) // Equivalent set-rule for `codly.file` codly.file-set_(..args) // Equivalent show rule for `codly.file` codly.file-show_(it => ...) body is required and may be supplied positionally; it is the displayed filename or filename content. The remaining fields are named. codly.new documents how code blocks derive and place this badge. codly.file-set_(..args) sets badge defaults in scope; codly.file-show_(it => ...) replaces each rendered badge with the callback's result. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body str | content Required, positional Displayed filename. fill none | paint luma(240) Background paint of the filename badge. stroke none | stroke 0.5pt + luma(160) Border stroke of the filename badge. inset length | dictionary (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em) Padding inside the filename badge. radius length | dictionary 2pt Corner radius of the filename badge. Behavior [!TIP] Pass a path to codly.new When the code input is a path, codly.new reads the file, derives the badge text from its basename, and uses its extension as the language when lang is omitted. Set file or lang explicitly to override those defaults. The badge is a box using fill, stroke, inset, and radius around body. A length applies uniformly; an inset dictionary sets padding by side or axis, and a radius dictionary sets individual corners. Example - type: slider name: example-radius label: Corner radius default: 4pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 - type: select name: fill label: Badge fill default: 'rgb("#d8eaff")' options: - label: Pale blue value: 'rgb("#d8eaff")' - label: Pale green value: 'rgb("#d9f5df")' - label: No fill value: 'none' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.file("src/main.typ", radius: example-radius, fill: fill)

title: header
text: codly.header Creates a configurable header element for a Codly code block. Signature // Create a header element codly.header( body, repeat: false, align: center + horizon, inset: auto, fill: luma(240), stroke: auto ) // Equivalent set-rule for `codly.header` codly.header-set_(..fields) // Equivalent show rule for `codly.header` codly.header-show_(it => ...) body is required and positional; all other fields are named. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Content displayed above the code rows. repeat none | bool false Whether the header repeats when the block spans multiple pages. align none | alignment center + horizon Alignment of the header cell content. inset none | length | dictionary | auto auto Header cell padding; auto inherits the grid inset. fill none | paint | auto luma(240) Header cell background, independent of code and number fills. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the default header fill. stroke none | stroke | auto auto Header cell border; auto inherits the grid stroke. Behavior [!TIP] Put the filename badge in the header codly.new places its file badge in the header by default. Supplying a custom header body keeps the badge alongside that body; style the badge separately with codly.file-set_(...). When used by codly.new, the header cell spans the code block's columns. repeat controls the underlying grid header's repetition. Setting fill to auto resolves to luma(240); the header fill is independent of line and number fills. The block's outer corner radius is configured on codly.new, not on the header element. codly.header-set_(..fields) sets defaults for headers in scope; codly.header-show_(replacement) installs a scoped replacement, whose callback receives the header element as it. Example - type: select name: example-fill label: Header fill default: 'rgb("#d8eaff")' options: - label: Pale blue value: 'rgb("#d8eaff")' - label: Pale green value: 'rgb("#d9f5df")' - label: No fill value: 'none' - type: slider name: example-radius label: Block corner radius default: 4pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py print('hello') ```, header: codly.header([*Greeting* · Python], fill: example-fill, inset: 5pt), radius: example-radius, )

title: footer
text: codly.footer Creates the footer element rendered below a code block. Signature // Create a footer element codly.footer( body, repeat: false, align: center + horizon, inset: auto, fill: none, stroke: auto ) // Equivalent set-rule for `codly.footer` codly.footer-set_(..args) // Equivalent show rule for `codly.footer` codly.footer-show_(it => ...) body is required and positional; all other fields are named. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Content displayed below the code rows. repeat none | bool false Whether the footer repeats when the block spans multiple pages. align none | alignment center + horizon Alignment of the footer cell content. inset none | length | dictionary | auto auto Footer cell padding; auto inherits the grid inset. fill none | paint | auto none Footer cell background, independent of code and number fills. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the default footer fill. stroke none | stroke | auto auto Footer cell border; auto inherits the grid stroke. Behavior [!NOTE] Footer fill defaults to none fill: auto resolves to the footer's default (none). Set an explicit fill when the footer should have a background; its fill is independent of line and number fills. Pass this element as the footer field of codly.new; plain content is also accepted there and wrapped with the defaults. A codly.footer-set_(...) rule supplies defaults, while fields set on an explicit codly.footer(...) take precedence. repeat controls whether the footer appears on continuation pages. codly.footer-show_(callback) applies a show rule to footer elements; the callback receives the element and returns replacement content. For example, #show: codly.footer-show_(it => [#it]) preserves the footer body. Example - type: select name: footer-fill label: Footer fill default: luma(240) options: - label: Light gray value: 'luma(240)' - label: Pale blue value: 'rgb("#e8f0ff")' - label: None value: 'none' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```js const ready = true; ```, footer: codly.footer([Generated output], fill: footer-fill, inset: 5pt), )

title: line
text: codly.line A generated row component that styles one displayed line in a Codly code block. Codly creates these rows while rendering codly.new; use the set/show wrappers here to configure their style. Signature codly.line(body, ..fields) body is required and positional. All other fields are named and optional. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional The raw.line content to render; generated row content is passed through unchanged. radius none | length 0.32em Corner radius used for the containing code grid. inset none | length | dictionary 0.32em Padding around each code row, as a length or a Typst inset dictionary. fill none | auto | paint | array<none | paint> | function (luma(240), none) Body-row paint, nonempty cycling palette, or row callback. The callback receives index, kind, source-line, and number; index is zero-based and includes header rows. auto restores the default palette, and whole-row highlights override this fill. stroke none | stroke 1pt + luma(240) Border stroke of the containing code grid. highlights none | array<highlight-config> none Character highlight configurations for displayed line numbers. Character bounds are zero-based with an exclusive end. smart-indent bool true Whether wrapped continuations retain indentation from the normalized source text. block-label none | label none Label of the containing block used to generate line and highlight references. reference none | dictionary none Internal displayed-number and suffix metadata for an unnumbered source line. Behavior [!TIP] Whole-line highlights win. A row's highlight fill takes precedence over the fill selected by this element, so use highlight styling when a highlighted line needs a distinct background. The fill callback receives a dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. index is zero-based in displayed-row order, including header, footer, skip, and callout rows — header and footer rows count toward it but do not invoke the callback. kind is "code", "skip", or "callout" for callback rows. source-line is the one-based source line for code and callout rows, and none for generated skip rows. number is the displayed line number, or none for unnumbered and generated rows. codly.line-set_(..args) sets row fields with show:; codly.line-show_(it => ...) replaces or wraps each generated row, receiving the row element as it. Example - type: slider name: row-green label: Code-row green channel default: 224 min: 0 max: 255 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.line-set_(fill: row => { if row.kind == "callout" { purple.lighten(80%) } else if row.kind == "code" { rgb(255, row-green, 190) } else { luma(238) } }) #codly.new( ```py let answer = 42 print(answer) ```, callouts: ((line: 1, body: [The value is set here.]),), )

title: number
text: codly.number A displayed line number in a Codly code block; number-set_ configures its style and number-show_ replaces its rendered content. Signature codly.number(number, parent, ..fields) number and parent are required positional fields; the remaining fields are named. Codly normally creates these elements while rendering codly.new. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning number none | content | int | array<int> Required, positional Displayed line number, number tuple, or replacement content; none leaves the cell empty. parent any Required, positional Containing raw-block value supplied by the code renderer. numbering str | function numbering.with("1") Numbering pattern or formatter applied to numeric values. align none | alignment left + horizon Alignment of the automatic number column. placement none | "inside" | "outside" "inside" Whether gutter columns appear inside or outside the code block border. fill none | auto | paint auto Number-column background; auto follows each body row's resolved fill. Behavior [!TIP] Custom content bypasses numbering. A content value is rendered as-is, while integer values go through numbering. Use an integer when you want the configured numbering style to apply. An integer is formatted with numbering; an array passes its values to the numbering function as separate arguments. A content value renders as-is, and number: none displays nothing. number-set_(..fields) sets scoped fields with #show:; number-show_(it => ...) replaces the generated number element with the callback's result. The placement setting applies to the number column for code blocks in scope. Outside placement also positions any configured gutters outside the code. Example - type: switch name: number-outside label: Place numbers outside default: false #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.number-set_(placement: if number-outside { "outside" } else { "inside" }) #codly.new( ```txt first line second line ```, )

title: highlight
text: codly.highlight codly.highlight renders a styled span over part of a source line in a Codly code block. Signature codly.highlight(body, highlight: highlight-config | none = none) codly.highlight-set_(..args) codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args) Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional The highlighted content. highlight none | highlight-config none Configuration record for the span, including its line, bounds, tag, and label. color paint | array<paint> Built-in palette Default paint or nonempty cycling palette. Whole-row and span highlights have independent per-block cycles; explicit paints do not consume a color. radius none | length 0.32em Corner radius of the highlight box. fill none | function (color) => color.lighten(80%) Function mapping the selected highlight color to a fill; none leaves the box unfilled. baseline none | length | auto 0pt Highlight box baseline shift; auto preserves the content's baseline. stroke none | stroke | function (color) => 0.5pt + color Border stroke, or a function mapping the selected highlight color to a stroke. inset none | length | dictionary 0.32em Padding inside the highlight box, as a length or a Typst inset dictionary. outset none | length | dictionary 0em Paint extent outside the highlight box, as a length or a Typst outset dictionary. clip none | bool true Whether to clip highlighted content to the box boundary. Behavior [!TIP] References need a labelled figure. A highlight label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically. [!NOTE] Source coordinates Highlight line numbers are one-indexed. Character offsets are zero-indexed, and end is exclusive. [!WARNING] A highlight palette must contain at least one color. An empty array causes a compilation error. Codly emits this element for spans declared in a code block's highlights field. Span positions are zero-indexed character offsets, with an exclusive end; line numbers are one-indexed. Bounds must be nonnegative; omitted or none bounds start at the beginning or extend through the end of the line. See codly.highlight-config for span metadata fields. Each code block has an independent highlight-paint cycle, separate from whole-line highlighting. A scalar color repeats for every span; an array cycles in declaration order. An explicit paint in the span metadata uses that paint without advancing the cycle, while its callback receives the next palette paint. The element's fill and stroke callbacks receive that resolved span paint. Per-span radius, clip, inset, outset, baseline, and stroke settings override the corresponding element fields when present. codly.highlight-set_(..args) sets fields for matching highlight elements in scope; codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the highlight element. Example - type: slider name: example-radius label: Corner radius default: 4pt unit: pt min: 0 max: 12 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.highlight-set_(radius: example-radius) #codly.new( ```py let answer = 42 ```, highlights: ((line: 1, start: 4, end: 10),), )

title: annotation
text: codly.annotation codly.annotation is the generated brace element displayed beside an annotated source-line range in a Codly code block. Signature // Create a new annotation. codly.annotation(body, ..fields) // Equivalent set-rule for an annotation. codly.annotation-set_(..args) // Override the show-rule for an annotation. codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args) Codly creates this element while rendering codly.new and supplies its fields. body is the required positional content field; the remaining fields are named. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Annotation content displayed after its number. label none | content Required, positional Internal reference marker content appended to the annotation; this field is not a Typst label. height none | length 0.0pt Resolved height of the spanned annotation cell, used to size the brace. num none | int 0 Automatic annotation number within the block. numbering none | function numbering.with("(1)") Annotation number formatter; none hides the number. Behavior [!TIP] References need a labelled figure. An annotation label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically. [!NOTE] Source coordinates Annotation ranges count one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive. Codly emits one annotation element for a configured line range. Range endpoints are one-indexed source-line positions, independent of displayed line-number offsets; annotation ranges cannot overlap. Use codly.annotation-config to configure a range. codly.annotation-set_(..args) sets fields on generated annotations in scope; codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the generated element. Example: Basic Usage - type: switch name: show-annotation-number label: Show annotation number default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py prepare() result = compute() print(result) cleanup() ```, annotations: (( start: 2, end: 4, content: [Computes and displays the result], numbering: if show-annotation-number { n => [(#n)] } else { none }, ),), )

title: bubble
text: codly.bubble A pointed callout bubble rendered next to a source line, with independent defaults for its paint, dimensions, spacing, and pointer. Signature // A codly pointed callout bubble. codly.bubble( body, gap: 0.5em, pointer-align: "center", pointer-size: 0.4em, pointer-height: auto, pointer-width: auto, pointer-offset: 0pt, align: center, fill: luma(245), stroke: 0.6pt + luma(80), inset: (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em), outset: 0pt, radius: 2pt, width: auto, line: int, pointer: int, placement: "below" ) codly.bubble is the generated element type for pointed callouts. Its body is positional; line and pointer are required named fields when representing the element directly. In normal use, create bubbles by setting pointer on a callouts entry. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body content Required, positional Content displayed inside the bubble. gap length | dictionary 0.5em Minimum horizontal and vertical separation between bubbles. A length sets both axes; omitted dictionary axes use 0.5em. pointer-align "start" | "center" | "end" "center" Preferred alignment of the bubble around its source character, clamped to the available row. pointer-size length 0.4em Default arrow height and half-base width. pointer-height length | auto auto Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. pointer-width length | auto auto Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. pointer-offset length 0pt Horizontal tip shift from the source character; positive moves right, negative moves left. Clamped to the bubble without moving its body. align alignment center Alignment of content inside the bubble, independent of grid cell alignment. fill none | paint luma(245) Fill shared by the bubble body and pointer. stroke none | stroke 0.6pt + luma(80) Stroke around the single bubble and pointer outline. inset length | dictionary (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em) Padding inside the bubble body. outset length | dictionary 0pt Additional painted extent around the padded body, reserved in the row. radius length 2pt Corner radius of the bubble body. width length | ratio | auto auto Preferred padded body width; auto fits the content within the available row. line int Required, named One-based source line to which the bubble is attached. pointer int Required, named One-based source character anchor; zero selects the line start. placement "above" | "below" "below" Whether the bubble appears above or below its source line. Behavior [!TIP] Bubbles can share a row Consecutive bubbles on the same side of a source line share a row when their outlines fit. If they collide, Codly places them in separate lanes in declaration order; adjust gap or width to control the spacing and wrapping. The bubble and arrow use one outline and fill. Content wraps at the available width. Negative dimensions, pointer sizes, insets, and outsets are rejected. Styling defaults set on codly.bubble are inherited by generated bubbles; explicit codly.callout settings and then entry-level bubble settings take precedence. A callout with pointer: none does not produce a bubble. Rules codly.bubble-set_(..args) sets styling defaults for generated bubbles. codly.bubble-show_(it, ..args) installs a show rule for generated bubbles; its first argument is replacement content or a callback. Example: Basic Usage - type: slider name: pointer label: Pointer position default: 17 min: 0 max: 26 step: 1 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.bubble-set_(fill: aqua.lighten(75%), radius: 6pt, width: 125pt) #codly.new( ```js let total = subtotal + tax ```, callouts: (( line: 1, pointer: pointer, body: [The final amount includes tax.], ),), ) Example: Custom Show Rule #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.bubble-show_(it => { box(stroke: red, it) }) #codly.new( ```js let total = subtotal + tax ```, callouts: (( line: 1, pointer: 17, body: [The final amount includes tax.], ),), )

title: callout
text: codly.callout A row attached to a source line in a Codly code block; it can be plain text or a pointed bubble. Signature // Create a new callout. codly.callout( body, line: int, align: auto, breakable: auto, inset: auto, fill: auto, stroke: auto, source-indent: false, placement: "below", // Parameters for the bubble if any. bubble-gap: auto, bubble-align: auto, bubble-fill: auto, bubble-stroke: auto, bubble-inset: auto, bubble-outset: auto, bubble-radius: auto, bubble-width: auto, // Parameters for the bubble's pointer if used. pointer: none, pointer-align: auto, pointer-size: auto, pointer-height: auto, pointer-width: auto, pointer-offset: auto, ) body is positional. line is required and named. Normally, callouts are created by entries in the callouts field; see codly.callout-config. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body content Required, positional Content displayed in the callout. line int Required, named One-based source line to which the callout is attached. align none | alignment | auto auto Grid cell alignment; auto inherits the grid alignment. breakable none | bool | auto auto Whether the cell can break across pages; auto inherits the grid setting. Pointed bubble groups remain together. inset none | length | dictionary | auto auto Grid cell padding; auto inherits the grid inset. fill none | paint | auto auto Grid cell background; auto inherits the body-row fill. stroke none | stroke | auto auto Grid cell border; auto inherits the grid stroke. source-indent bool false Whether plain callouts retain source indentation and reserve the gutter columns. Pointed bubbles keep their character anchors. placement "above" | "below" "below" Whether the callout appears above or below its source line. bubble-gap length | dictionary | auto auto Minimum horizontal and vertical separation between bubbles. A length sets both axes; omitted dictionary axes use 0.5em. pointer none | int none One-based character anchor in the source line; zero selects the line start. none disables the pointed bubble. pointer-align "start" | "center" | "end" | auto auto Preferred alignment of the bubble around its source character, clamped to the available row. pointer-size length | auto auto Default arrow height and half-base width. pointer-height length | auto auto Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. pointer-width length | auto auto Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. pointer-offset length | auto auto Horizontal tip shift from the source character; positive moves right, negative moves left. Clamped to the bubble without moving its body. bubble-align alignment | auto auto Alignment of content inside the bubble, independent of grid cell alignment. bubble-fill none | paint | auto auto Fill shared by the bubble body and pointer. bubble-stroke none | stroke | auto auto Stroke around the single bubble and pointer outline. bubble-inset length | dictionary | auto auto Padding inside the bubble body. bubble-outset length | dictionary | auto auto Additional painted extent around the padded body, reserved in the row. bubble-radius length | auto auto Corner radius of the bubble body. bubble-width length | ratio | auto auto Preferred padded body width; auto fits the content within the available row. Behavior [!TIP] Plain callouts can follow source indentation Set source-indent: true to align a plain callout with the source indentation while preserving the gutter columns. Pointed callouts stay anchored to their source character. Callout lines are source-line coordinates, unaffected by displayed line-number offsets. Pointer positions count characters in the source line, with zero denoting its start; the pointer follows the rendered character when code wraps. Negative pointers, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are rejected. A bubble's body and arrow share one fill and outline, and bubble text wraps to its available width. Unspecified or auto bubble styling inherits from codly.bubble, after explicit codly.callout styling. Entry values in callouts take precedence over the element's set-rule values. Explicit none disables bubble fill or stroke; pointer: none keeps a callout plain. codly.callout-set_(..args) sets defaults for callout cells and bubbles; codly.callout-show_(it, ..args) installs a show rule taking replacement content or a callback such as it => [#it]. Bubble-specific defaults and show rules are documented on codly.bubble. Example - type: switch name: source-indent label: Align plain callout to source indentation default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.callout-set_(source-indent: source-indent) #codly.new( ```py if ready: start() ```, callouts: ( (line: 1, body: [Plain callout aligned with the source.]), (line: 2, pointer: 3, body: [Pointing at `start`.]), ), )

title: ref
text: codly.ref [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure. Line, highlight, and annotation references require the code block to sit inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically. Sets shared formatting for references to code lines, highlights, and annotations. Signature codly.ref(body, by: "line", sep: "-", numbering: numbering.with("1")) codly.ref-set_(..fields) codly.ref is an element definition; codly.ref-set_(...) is a set-rule wrapper for its fields, not a separate element. There is no ref-show_: references render through native syntax and the show rules of the generated reference elements. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional The reference content. by none | "line" | "item" "line" Reference mode: "line" displays the line number; "item" displays the highlight tag or annotation content. sep none | str | content "-" Separator between the containing block reference and the referenced line or item. numbering none | function numbering.with("1") Line-number formatter used when by is "line"; none hides the line-number part. Behavior [!TIP] Choose what the reference shows. The shared by: "line" setting shows the displayed line number. by: "item" shows the highlight tag or annotation content instead. [!WARNING] Item references to highlights need a tag. When by: "item", each referenced highlight must define a tag; Codly reports an error if the tag is missing. Annotation item references use the annotation's content. The fields in codly.ref are shared defaults for codly.line-ref, codly.highlight-ref, and codly.annotation-ref. A field set directly on one of those generated reference elements takes precedence over the shared setting. by: "item" uses the highlight's tag or the annotation's content; line references always refer to a displayed line. Numbering callbacks receive the displayed line number. These references resolve to the containing code figure or block, so ordinary Typst reference formatting still applies to that target. See codly.line-ref, codly.highlight-ref, and codly.annotation-ref for the generated reference fields. Example This figure labels a code block and an annotation. The reference to the annotation uses its content as the item suffix: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ") #figure(caption: [A code example])[ #codly.new( ``` first line second line ```, annotations: ((start: 2, label: <note>, content: [the note]),), ) ]<example> The annotation reference is @note and the line is @example:2.

title: line-ref
text: codly.line-ref [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure. Put the code block inside a labelled figure to enable line references. Codly detects that figure label automatically, so omit the block-label argument from codly.new. Formats native Typst references to displayed lines in labeled Codly code blocks.
