Signature codly.line-ref(body, block: label, number: int, suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto) codly.line-ref-set_(..args) codly.line-ref-show_(it, ..args) codly.line-ref is a generated element definition; Codly creates it for line targets, so user code normally refers to those targets with @block:line rather than constructing the element. line-ref-set_(...) applies field defaults to generated line references in the current scope. line-ref-show_(it) installs a show rule; its first argument is the replacement callback or content, not field overrides. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Internal reference body. block label Required, named Label of the containing code block or figure. number int Required, named Displayed line number after offsets and skips. suffix none | content none Suffix identifying an unnumbered line relative to the preceding displayed number. separator none | auto | str | content auto Separator after the block reference; auto inherits codly.ref.sep. numbering none | auto | function auto Line-number formatter; auto inherits codly.ref.numbering, and none hides the line number. Behavior The constructor is exported, but references are normally generated from native @block:line syntax; the element has no custom casts and cannot itself carry a label. The reference shows the block figure followed by the formatted line number — the displayed number, not a source position. separator: auto and numbering: auto inherit codly.ref's sep and numbering settings. Explicit fields set through line-ref-set_ override those shared defaults for line references in scope. A numbering function receives the displayed line number. line-ref-show_ lets a show rule replace or wrap the generated reference; its callback receives the element. See codly.ref for shared reference defaults. Example Labels a code block and refers to its second displayed line; the local set rule changes the separator and number format: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.line-ref-set_(separator: " line ", numbering: n => [L#n]) #figure(caption: [A small code block])[ #codly.new( ``` first line second line ```, ) ]<example> The reference points to line two of the block: @example:2.

title: highlight-ref
text: codly.highlight-ref [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure. A highlight label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure. codly.highlight-ref declares the native reference element emitted for a labelled highlight. Signature // Create a highlight reference element codly.highlight-ref( body, block: label, line: int, by: "line" | "item", item: content | none = none, separator: auto | str | content = auto, numbering: auto | function | none = auto ) // Set default fields for matching highlight references codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args) // Install a replacement callback or content for matching highlight references codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args) Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Internal reference body. block label Required, named Label of the containing code block or figure. line int Required, named Displayed line number containing the highlight. item none | content none Highlight tag displayed when by is "item". by "line" | "item" Required, named Whether the reference displays the line number or highlight tag. separator none | auto | str | content auto Separator after the block reference; auto inherits codly.ref.sep. numbering none | auto | function auto Line-number formatter; auto inherits codly.ref.numbering, and none hides the line number. Behavior Typst emits this element when a native reference targets a label on a highlight. It retains the reference to the containing figure or code block, so native figure numbering and links work. With by: "line", the formatter receives the displayed line number. With by: "item", the tag is shown and item must be present. A none formatter suppresses the numeric part of line references; item references still show their tag. The default separator and formatter come from codly.ref. codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args) sets fields for matching references; codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the reference element. Example #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.highlight-ref-set_(numbering: numbering.with("H1")) The marked line is @marked. #figure(caption: [A labelled highlight])[ #codly.new( ``` answer = 42 ```, highlights: ((line: 1, start: 0, end: 6, label: <marked>),), ) ]<listing>

title: annotation-ref
text: codly.annotation-ref [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure. An annotation label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure. A native reference element created for a labelled annotation in a code block inside a figure. Signature // Create a new annotation reference. codly.annotation-ref(body, block: label, line: int, item: content, by: "line" | "item", suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto) // Equivalent set-rule for an annotation reference. codly.annotation-ref-set_(..args) // Override the show-rule for an annotation reference. codly.annotation-ref-show_(it, ..args) Codly creates this element when Typst resolves a native reference such as @note. Use annotation-ref-set_(...) to set fields in scope, or annotation-ref-show_(callback) to replace or transform its display. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body none | content Required, positional Internal reference body. block label Required, named Label of the containing code block or figure. line int Required, named Displayed number of the first line covered by the annotation. item content Required, named Annotation content or automatic annotation number displayed when by is "item". suffix none | content none Suffix identifying an unnumbered start line. by "line" | "item" Required, named Whether the reference displays the line number or annotation item. separator none | auto | str | content auto Separator after the block reference; auto inherits codly.ref.sep. numbering none | auto | function auto Line-number formatter; auto inherits codly.ref.numbering, and none hides the line number. by, separator, and numbering can also be set for all generated references with codly.ref. Explicit fields on this element take precedence. In item mode, the annotation's content is used; numbering and suffix apply only to line mode. With line mode and numbering: none, the rendered reference contains just the native reference to the code block. annotation-ref-show_ receives the generated reference element, so a callback can inspect or wrap it. For example, #show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: #it]) prefixes each displayed annotation reference while keeping its existing rendering. Example: Basic usage With the default line mode, the reference appends the displayed line number to the figure reference: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #figure(caption: [A code example])[ #codly.new( ``` first line second line ```, annotations: ((start: 2, label: <note>, content: [the note]),), ) ]<example> The annotation reference is @note. Example: Item-based reference With by: "item", the suffix is the annotation's content; the show rule adds a prefix: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ") #show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: #it]) #figure(caption: [A code example])[ #codly.new( ``` first line second line ```, annotations: ((start: 2, label: <note>, content: [the note]),), ) ]<example> The annotation reference is @note.

title: sublang-block
text: codly.sublang-block [!WARNING] Sublang blocks cost performance. Each sublang block requires re-parsing and introspection; heavy use slows compilation. The generated element that holds one syntax-highlighted language range inside a Codly code block. Signature codly.sublang-block(body, idx) Codly creates this element while rendering codly.new. In normal use, configure language ranges with the block's sublangs field and codly.sublang, rather than constructing this element directly. Both required fields are positional in the generated element constructor. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning body content Required, positional Raw block used to resolve syntax styling for the sublanguage range. idx int Required, positional Zero-based index of the sublanguage configuration within the block. Behavior [!NOTE] Range indexes follow declaration order. idx is zero-based within one code block's sublangs array; it does not identify a source line or language key. For each configured sublanguage range, Codly creates a raw block with that range's language and stores it in body. Its display keeps the syntax highlighting while attaching per-line metadata so the block renderer can reuse it. Example #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```sh > cat test.rs fn main() { println!("hello"); } > exit ```, sublangs: ((start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"),), )

title: Types
text: Types Types describe configuration values used by components. Each page lists fields, defaults, validation, and accepted shorthand forms. [!NOTE] Source coordinates Ranges and annotations use source-line positions. Whole-line highlights use displayed line numbers, which can change with offsets and skipped lines. Check each type's coordinate rules before combining these features. codly.language codly.range codly.skip codly.highlighted-line codly.unnumbered-line codly.smart-skip codly.highlight-config codly.annotation-config codly.callout-config codly.gutter-column codly.diff codly.sublang codly.rainbow codly.indent-guides

title: language
text: codly.language Defines the displayed name, color, and optional icon for a language badge in a code block. Signature codly.language( name: str | content, color: paint | none = none, icon: str | content | none = none, ) name is required and named. Fields expecting this type also accept a string as shorthand for name, or a dictionary. Unknown fields are retained. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning name str | content Required, named Displayed language name. color none | paint none Language color; none uses codly.lang.default-color. icon none | str | content none Language icon; none hides the icon. The declaration preserves additional, unknown fields. They can provide language-specific overrides to codly.lang fields, such as radius or fill. Behavior Use language definitions as values in the languages dictionary passed to codly.lang-set_. The dictionary key must match the raw block's language tag. The settings apply within the show rule's scope. A definition's name, icon, and color customize the badge; an omitted definition falls back to the raw language tag. A definition's matching codly.lang style fields override the corresponding settings supplied to codly.lang-set_. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.lang-set_(languages: ( rs: (name: [Rust], color: rgb("b7502a"), icon: "R"), )) #show raw.where(block: true): codly.new ```rs fn main() { println!("Hello, Rust!"); } ```

title: range
text: codly.range Selects an inclusive range of one-indexed source lines for a code block. Signature codly.range(start, end: none) start is positional and required. end is optional and may be passed positionally or by name. Parameters Field Type Default / required Meaning start int Required, positional First source line of the range, one-based. end none | int none, positional Last source line, inclusive; none selects the remainder of the block. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates Range endpoints count source lines from one and include both start and end; displayed numbering offsets do not change them. [!TIP] Adjacent ranges merge. When several ranges are selected, Codly sorts them and merges overlapping or directly adjacent ranges before rendering. Pass a range to codly.new's range field, or pass several ranges to its ranges field. An open range such as codly.range(3) continues through the final source line. The constructor accepts positional arguments (codly.range(2, 4)) or named arguments (codly.range(start: 2, end: 4)). Implicit casts accept a one- or two-element array or a dictionary with start and optional end keys; unknown dictionary keys are rejected. Bounds are type-checked as integers (or none for end), with no positivity or ordering constraint. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ``` prepare() validate() transform() save() ```, range: codly.range(2, 3), )

title: skip
text: codly.skip Describes an explicit collapsed gap in a code block; pass it in codly.new's skips field. Signature codly.skip(position, length: 1) position is the required positional argument; length is optional and can be supplied positionally or by name. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning position int Required, positional One-based source line before which the omission row is inserted. length int 1, positional Number of omitted lines added to subsequent displayed line numbers. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates position is a one-indexed source line, even when ranges or offsets change which lines appear. Position 2 inserts the gap before source line 2. [!TIP] Duplicate positions make one skip row. If multiple skips have the same position, Codly uses the first entry's length to adjust subsequent displayed line numbers. The constructor accepts codly.skip(position, length) or named fields. A dictionary casts using position and optional length; an array of one or two values casts positionally. The skips field sorts entries by position. Explicit skips represent lines already omitted from the supplied source. They add a gap row and increase subsequent displayed numbers; they do not remove source lines. Use range or ranges with smart-skip to omit lines that are still present. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```text first second third fourth ```, skips: (codly.skip(2, 4),), )

title: highlighted-line
text: codly.highlighted-line Describes one whole line to highlight in codly.new. Signature codly.highlighted-line(line, color: none) line is required and positional; color is optional and positional or named. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning line int Required, positional Displayed line number to highlight, including offsets and skips. color none | paint none, positional Explicit background paint; none uses the next default highlight color transformed by codly.highlight.fill. Behavior [!NOTE] Uses displayed line numbers line refers to the number shown in the document, including offsets and numbering changes from skips. A source line with no displayed number cannot be selected this way. [!TIP] Explicit colors leave the palette cycle untouched A supplied color is used directly. Entries with color: none take and advance the next codly.highlight palette color. The constructor also accepts named fields. The value casts from an integer, a dictionary with line and optional color, or an array of one or two values in field order; other values and array lengths fail to cast. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```text prepare() run() cleanup() ```, highlighted: (codly.highlighted-line(2, yellow.lighten(75%)),), )

title: unnumbered-line
text: codly.unnumbered-line Selects a source line to show without its line number, optionally putting content in the number cell. Signature codly.unnumbered-line(line, fill: []) Both arguments are positional: line is required and fill is optional. Parameters Field Type Default / required Meaning line int Required, positional One-based source line to leave unnumbered. fill content [], positional Content displayed instead of the automatic line number. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates line is a one-indexed source line, even when a range or offset changes its displayed position or number. Pass entries to codly.new's unnumbered field. The constructor takes positional arguments; implicit casts accept an integer, a one- or two-element array, or a dictionary with line and optional fill fields. An unnumbered line does not advance the displayed number sequence, so later numbered lines remain contiguous. Consecutive unnumbered lines can be referenced with labels such as @block:l2p1 and @block:l2p2, where the l number is the preceding displayed number and p counts the unnumbered lines after it. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #figure(caption: [Unnumbered source lines])[ #codly.new( ``` first label: second end last ```, unnumbered: ( codly.unnumbered-line(2, [↳]), codly.unnumbered-line(4), ), ) ]<block> The unnumbered lines are @block:l1p1 and @block:l2p1.

title: smart-skip
text: codly.smart-skip Configures which omitted source-line gaps appear as collapsed skip rows when a code block displays selected ranges. Signature codly.smart-skip( first: bool | none = none, last: bool | none = none, rest: bool | none = none, ) All fields are named and optional. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning first none | bool none Whether to display an omission row before the first selected range. last none | bool none Whether to display an omission row after the last selected range. rest none | bool none Whether to display omission rows between disjoint selected ranges. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates Automatic skips mark gaps between displayed source ranges; they do not change the source-line coordinates used by those ranges. Pass this value to codly.new's smart-skip field. A boolean casts to the same value for all three fields. A dictionary casts to this type: omitted rest defaults to false, and omitted first or last inherits rest. Thus (rest: true, first: false) enables middle skips and trailing skips, while suppressing a leading skip. With all three fields false, no automatic skips are inserted. A skip row is inserted only for a discontinuity in the displayed source lines; its represented length is the number of omitted lines. Example: Basic Usage - type: switch name: show-middle-gap label: Show the omitted middle lines default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```python def prepare(): load_data() validate() transform() save() report() cleanup() ```, ranges: ((2, 3), (6, 7)), smart-skip: codly.smart-skip(first: false, last: false, rest: show-middle-gap), )

title: highlight-config
text: codly.highlight-config Describes one character-level highlight on a source line in a Codly code block. See codly.new for the block's highlights field. Signature codly.highlight-config(line, start: none, end: none, fill: none, tag: none, inset: none, baseline: none, clip: none, outset: none, radius: none, label: none, stroke: none, depth: none) line is the required positional field; every other field is named. A dictionary with a line key can also be cast to this type. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning line int Required, positional Positive displayed line number, including offsets and inserted skips. start none | int none Inclusive zero-based character boundary; none selects the line start. end none | int none Exclusive zero-based character boundary; none selects the line end. fill none | paint | function none Explicit paint or a callback receiving the next default palette paint. Explicit paints do not consume a palette color; callbacks do. none uses the palette. tag none | str | content none Optional content displayed beside the highlighted span. inset none | length | dictionary none Override for codly.highlight.inset. baseline none | length | auto none Override for the highlight box baseline; auto preserves the content's baseline. clip none | bool none Override for codly.highlight.clip. outset none | length | dictionary none Override for codly.highlight.outset. radius none | length none Override for codly.highlight.radius. label none | label none Label for a native highlight reference when the containing block has a block-label. stroke none | stroke | function none Override for codly.highlight.stroke. depth none | int none Highlight nesting depth. The renderer derives and replaces this value from span containment. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates line is a one-indexed displayed line number, including any offset. start and end are zero-indexed character positions, and end is exclusive. [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure To reference a highlight, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure. The constructor and dictionary cast normalize omitted or none bounds to start: 0 and an end bound covering the rest of the line. Explicit bounds must be nonnegative; line must be positive. Character positions are zero-indexed and the end is exclusive, unlike the inclusive, one-indexed source-line ranges. A fill paint is used directly and does not consume a palette entry; a callback receives the next palette paint. Highlights using none also consume the next palette entry. An empty configured palette is invalid. Local style fields override the corresponding codly.highlight settings when provided. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py let answer = 42 ```, highlights: (codly.highlight-config(1, start: 4, end: 10, fill: yellow.lighten(65%), tag: "value"),), )

title: annotation-config
text: codly.annotation-config Describes an annotation attached to one or more one-indexed source lines in a code block. Signature codly.annotation-config(start, end: none, content: none, label: none, numbering: numbering.with("(1)")) Parameters Field Type Default / required Meaning start int Required, positional First covered source line, one-based and positive. end none | int none Last covered source line, inclusive; none selects start only. content none | content none Annotation content; none displays only its automatic number. label none | label none Label for a native annotation reference when the containing block has a block-label. numbering none | function numbering.with("(1)") Automatic annotation number formatter; none hides the number. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates start and end are one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive. Displayed line-number offsets do not change the covered source lines. [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure To reference an annotation, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure. Codly discovers the figure label automatically. [!WARNING] Annotation ranges cannot overlap. Two annotations cannot cover the same source line. Because end is inclusive, the next annotation must start after the previous one's end. The positional start argument is required. The constructor also accepts a dictionary with a start key. Dictionary and constructor inputs are type-checked, then normalized: a missing or none end becomes start, and missing content becomes none. start and a supplied end must be positive, and end must not precede start. Annotations are passed in the code block's annotations array. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py prepare() result = compute() print(result) cleanup() ```, annotations: ( codly.annotation-config( 2, end: 3, content: [These lines compute and display the result.], ), ), )

title: callout-config
text: codly.callout-config Describes a content row attached to a source line in a code block. Use it in the callouts field of codly.new. Signature codly.callout-config(line: int, body: content, align: auto, breakable: auto, inset: auto, fill: auto, stroke: auto, source-indent: auto, placement: auto, bubble-gap: auto, pointer: auto, pointer-align: auto, pointer-size: auto, pointer-height: auto, pointer-width: auto, pointer-offset: auto, bubble-align: auto, bubble-fill: auto, bubble-stroke: auto, bubble-inset: auto, bubble-outset: auto, bubble-radius: auto, bubble-width: auto) All fields are named. A dictionary with line and body keys can also be used as a callout entry. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning line int Required, named Attached source line, one-based and positive. body content Required, named Content displayed in the callout. align none | alignment | auto auto Cell alignment; auto inherits the codly.callout setting. breakable none | bool | auto auto Whether the cell can break across pages; auto inherits the codly.callout setting. inset none | length | dictionary | auto auto Cell padding; auto inherits the codly.callout setting. fill none | paint | auto auto Cell background; auto inherits the codly.callout setting. stroke none | stroke | auto auto Cell border; auto inherits the codly.callout setting. source-indent bool | auto auto Whether plain callouts retain source indentation and reserve the gutter columns. Pointed bubbles keep their character anchors. placement "above" | "below" | auto auto Whether the callout appears above or below its source line. bubble-gap length | dictionary | auto auto Minimum horizontal and vertical separation between bubbles. A length sets both axes; omitted dictionary axes use 0.5em. pointer none | int | auto auto One-based character anchor in the source line; zero selects the line start. none disables the pointed bubble. pointer-align "start" | "center" | "end" | auto auto Preferred alignment of the bubble around its source character, clamped to the available row. pointer-size length | auto auto Default arrow height and half-base width. pointer-height length | auto auto Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. pointer-width length | auto auto Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. pointer-offset length | auto auto Horizontal tip shift from the source character; positive moves right, negative moves left. Clamped to the bubble without moving its body. bubble-align alignment | auto auto Alignment of content inside the bubble, independent of grid cell alignment. bubble-fill none | paint | auto auto Fill shared by the bubble body and pointer. bubble-stroke none | stroke | auto auto Stroke around the single bubble and pointer outline. bubble-inset length | dictionary | auto auto Padding inside the bubble body. bubble-outset length | dictionary | auto auto Additional painted extent around the padded body, reserved in the row. bubble-radius length | auto auto Corner radius of the bubble body. bubble-width length | ratio | auto auto Preferred padded body width; auto fits the content within the available row. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates line is a one-indexed source line. pointer is a one-indexed character position after any diff marker is removed; 0 points to the start of the line. [!WARNING] Pointed bubble groups stay together Bubbles attached to a source line stay together on one page, so a group may move as a unit at a page break. An entry's auto style values inherit from codly.callout; bubble styles can then inherit from codly.bubble. Explicit entry values take precedence. Cell fill and stroke accept none to disable painting. A pointed bubble uses one shared outline and paint for its body and arrow, and wraps its content at the available width. Pointer positions count characters in the source line after a diff marker is removed; unlike highlight bounds, they are one-indexed, with zero denoting the start. The pointer follows the rendered character when source text wraps. Consecutive bubbles on the same side with matching cell styles share a row when their outlines fit; overlaps use another lane in declaration order. Negative pointer positions, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are invalid. bubble-gap dictionaries accept only x and y, whose omitted values default to 0.5em. Example: Basic Usage - type: slider name: bubble-width label: Bubble width default: 120pt unit: pt min: 80 max: 180 step: 10 #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py if ready: start() ```, callouts: ( codly.callout-config( line: 2, pointer: 5, body: [This call runs when the input is ready.], bubble-width: bubble-width, bubble-fill: aqua.lighten(80%), ), ), )

title: gutter-column
text: codly.gutter-column Defines one independently styled column beside a code block. Use it in gutters to show source-line labels, markers, or other row-specific content. Signature codly.gutter-column( values: array<none | str | int | float | content> | function, width: auto | length | ratio | fraction = auto, align: auto | alignment = auto, inset: auto | length | dictionary = auto, stroke: auto | stroke | dictionary | none = auto, fill: auto | paint | array<paint | none> | function | none = auto, text: dictionary = (:), ) values is required and named. Arrays and functions can also be passed directly as gutter column specifications; dictionaries are cast to this type. Parameters Field Type Default / required Meaning values array<none | str | int | float | content> | function Required, named Source-line values or a callback receiving index, kind, source-line, number, and text. Short arrays and none entries leave cells empty; generated rows have no source text. width auto | length | ratio | fraction auto Nonnegative column width; auto sizes to its content. align auto | alignment auto Cell alignment; auto inherits the grid number alignment. inset auto | length | dictionary auto Cell padding; auto inherits the grid number inset. stroke none | auto | stroke | dictionary auto Cell border; auto inherits the grid stroke, and none disables it. fill none | auto | paint | array<none | paint> | function auto Cell background, nonempty cycling palette, or row callback. auto follows the body-row fill; none leaves the cell unfilled. text dictionary (:) Text settings applied to the column content. Behavior [!NOTE] Array values follow source lines An array entry at index 0 supplies source line 1, even with ranges or offsets. Missing entries and none leave the gutter cell empty. [!TIP] Use a callback for rendered-row logic Only code and skip rows have gutter cells. A callback receives both source-line and kind, so it can handle skip rows separately from code. A callback receives the rendered row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, number, and text. index counts displayed rows, including headers and callouts; source-line is one-based for source rows and none for generated rows. Callbacks may return content, strings, numbers, or none. Values are validated when resolved, and width must be non-negative. auto alignment and insets inherit the number column's settings; fill: auto follows the body row. A fill callback also receives the row dictionary, with text populated from the source line where available. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ``` let answer = 42 print(answer) ```, gutters: ( codly.gutter-column( values: row => if row.kind == "code" { str(row.source-line) + ". " + row.text } else { none }, align: right, inset: (left: 4pt, right: 8pt), fill: gray.lighten(90%), ), ), )

title: diff
text: codly.diff Configures automatic parsing, syntax highlighting, gutters, and row fills for raw blocks whose language is diff-<language> or diff,<language>. Signature codly.diff( enabled: bool = true, added-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("dafbe1"), removed-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ffebe9"), meta-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ddf4ff"), context-fill: auto | paint | function = auto, numbers: bool = true, markers: bool = true, added-marker: str | content = "+", removed-marker: str | content = "−", old-offset: int = 0, new-offset: int = 0, ) The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning enabled bool true Whether to process diff-prefixed code. added-fill none | auto | paint | function rgb("dafbe1") Added-row background. auto follows the ordinary row fill; none leaves it unfilled. A callback receives the row and its diff record. removed-fill none | auto | paint | function rgb("ffebe9") Removed-row background. auto follows the ordinary row fill; none leaves it unfilled. A callback receives the row and its diff record. meta-fill none | auto | paint | function rgb("ddf4ff") Patch metadata background. auto follows the ordinary row fill; none leaves it unfilled. A callback receives the row and its diff record. context-fill none | auto | paint | function auto Unchanged-row background. auto follows the ordinary row fill; none leaves it unfilled. A callback receives the row and its diff record. numbers bool true Whether the default diff gutters display old and new line numbers. markers bool true Whether the default diff gutters display change markers. added-marker str | content "+" Marker displayed beside an added line. removed-marker str | content "−" Marker displayed beside a removed line. old-offset int 0 Additional offset applied to old-side gutter numbers. new-offset int 0 Additional offset applied to new-side gutter numbers. Behavior [!TIP] Use the patch language prefix Set the raw block language to diff-<language> or diff,<language>, such as diff-py or diff,py, to enable patch parsing and highlight the changed code as Python. [!NOTE] Patch line coordinates References and line-based settings use displayed patch-row numbers. Highlight and callout character positions count code after the diff marker is removed. [!WARNING] Combined merge diffs are unsupported Codly parses unified patches, including multiple files and hunks, but not combined merge diff format. With the block-level diff setting at auto (the default), Codly detects both prefixes and strips them for syntax highlighting. Old and new source views are rendered separately, so removed code does not affect new-side syntax state. Unified patches may contain multiple files and hunks, each highlighted independently. A non-patch snippet may use , +, and - prefixes for context, added, and removed rows. For fenced blocks, diff-py works in Typst 0.15; use raw(..., lang: "diff,py") on versions without comma support in language tags. Each fill accepts a paint, none, or auto; auto uses the ordinary row fill. A callback receives the row with a diff record containing kind, old, and new line coordinates, as well as the row's usual fields. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff fills. Setting diff: false or diff: none disables processing; setting it to true enables the default configuration. Custom gutters replace the automatic old/new/marker columns. Example: Basic Usage - type: switch name: diff-enabled label: Process the diff default: true #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```diff-py shared -old = 1 +new = 2 tail ```, diff: if diff-enabled { auto } else { false }, )

title: sublang
text: codly.sublang Assigns a syntax-highlighting language to an inclusive range of source lines in a code block. Signature codly.sublang( start: int, end: int, lang: str, ) All fields are required and named. The value can also be supplied as a dictionary. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning start int Required, named First source line of the range, one-based and positive. end int Required, named Last source line of the range, inclusive and at least start. lang str Required, named Syntax-highlighting language key. Behavior [!NOTE] Source coordinates Sublanguage ranges count one-indexed source lines and include both endpoints, independent of displayed line-number offsets. [!TIP] Highlighting preserves the original lines. Codly applies each range's syntax language to its source lines while keeping their text and positions in the outer code block. Pass one or more codly.sublang values in the sublangs argument to codly.new. start must be positive and end at least start; invalid ranges raise an error. Lines outside the ranges keep the raw block's language. Ranges may also be supplied as dictionaries with the same three fields. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```sh echo before fn answer() { 42 } echo after ```, sublangs: ( (start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"), ), )

title: rainbow
text: codly.rainbow Configures syntax-aware coloring for matching code delimiters by nesting depth. Signature codly.rainbow( enabled: bool = true, palette: array<color> = (...), pairs: array<"()" | "[]" | "{}"> = ("()", "[]", "{}"), depth-offset: int = 0, unmatched: color | none = none, code-scopes: str = ..., ignore-scopes: str = ..., ) The value can also be a dictionary with these fields, or a boolean that sets enabled. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning enabled bool true Whether to color delimiters. palette array<color> Built-in palette Colors repeated at successive nesting depths; must not be empty. pairs array<"()" | "[]" | "{}"> ("()", "[]", "{}") Delimiter pairs that contribute to nesting. depth-offset int 0 Nonnegative offset into the palette. unmatched none | color none Color for unmatched delimiters, or none to preserve their syntax style. code-scopes str Built-in selectors Syntax scope selectors identifying code in the private classification theme. ignore-scopes str Built-in selectors Syntax scope selectors excluding literals and comments. Behavior [!WARNING] The palette must be nonempty. An empty palette or a negative depth-offset causes a compilation error. [!TIP] Adjust scopes for unusual grammars. code-scopes and ignore-scopes replace the built-in selectors. Customize them when a language classifies delimiters differently from the defaults. Set rainbow on codly.new or in codly.set_ to configure blocks in that scope. true enables the defaults and false disables the pass. Delimiters are colored according to nesting depth, cycling through palette; depth-offset shifts the starting color. Only pairs listed in pairs contribute to nesting. Unclosed openers and unmatched closers use unmatched when it is a color; otherwise they retain their syntax highlighting. The pass uses syntax scopes to find code and ignore literals and comments; sublanguage regions are processed with their own nesting stack. Example: Basic Usage - type: switch name: rainbow-enabled label: Color delimiters default: true - type: select name: rainbow-pairs label: Delimiter pairs default: '("()", "[]", "{}")' options: - label: All pairs value: '("()", "[]", "{}")' - label: Braces only value: '("{}",)' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```rs fn main() { let items = [1, 2, 3]; println!("{}", items[0]); } ```, rainbow: if rainbow-enabled { (palette: (rgb("#d73a49"), rgb("#005cc5"), rgb("#22863a")), pairs: rainbow-pairs) } else { false }, )

title: indent-guides
text: codly.indent-guides Configures optional vertical guides at complete indentation levels in a code block. Signature codly.indent-guides( enabled: bool = true, width: auto | int = auto, blank-lines: bool = true, rainbow: auto | bool = auto, palette: auto | array<color> = auto, depth-offset: auto | int = auto, color: color = luma(70%), thickness: length = 0.5pt, x-offset: length = 0pt, ) The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled. Fields Field Type Default / required Meaning enabled bool true Whether to draw indentation guides. width auto | int auto Spaces per level; auto votes on observed indentation changes. blank-lines bool true Continue shared levels across interior blank lines. rainbow auto | bool auto Color guides by level; auto follows delimiter rainbow enablement. palette auto | array<color> auto Nonempty guide palette; auto shares the delimiter palette. depth-offset auto | int auto Nonnegative palette offset; auto shares the delimiter offset. color color luma(70%) Guide color when rainbow guides are disabled. thickness length 0.5pt Positive guide stroke thickness. x-offset length 0pt Horizontal shift of every guide; positive moves right, negative moves left. Supports em lengths. Behavior [!TIP] Check the inferred indentation step width: auto chooses the most frequently observed change in leading spaces; ties favor the smaller step, and no observed step falls back to four spaces. Set width explicitly when the source uses a known indentation size. [!NOTE] Only complete levels get guides A guide is drawn for each complete width-sized level. Indentation that does not reach the next complete level has no guide. Set the block-level indent-guides field to true for defaults, false to disable inherited guides for one block, or a configuration to customize them. Interior blank lines continue only the levels shared by the surrounding nonblank lines when blank-lines is true; leading and trailing blank lines have no inferred guides. With rainbow: auto, guides use delimiter rainbow colors when delimiter rainbow is enabled. Explicit rainbow: true enables palette coloring; false uses color. An explicit palette or depth offset overrides values inherited from delimiter rainbow settings. The palette must not be empty, width must be positive or auto, depth offset must be nonnegative or auto, and thickness must be positive. Invalid field types are rejected by the declared types. Guides follow source indentation and extend across wrapped visual rows when smart indentation is enabled. x-offset shifts all guides horizontally without changing source columns. Example: Basic Usage - type: switch name: guides-enabled label: Show indentation guides default: true - type: select name: guide-width label: Spaces per level default: '4' options: - label: Two spaces value: '2' - label: Four spaces value: '4' - label: Eight spaces value: '8' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```text root child leaf sibling root ```, indent-guides: if guides-enabled { (width: guide-width) } else { false }, )

title: Themes and helpers
text: Themes and helpers Use themes to apply consistent component styles and info to inspect a labelled block in context. [!TIP] Apply themes in scope. Use #show: codly.theme(...) before the code blocks you want to style. Put the rule inside a content block to limit it to that part of the document. codly.theme codly.themes codly.define-theme codly.info

title: theme
text: codly.theme Returns scoped set and show rules that apply a built-in or custom theme to Codly elements. Signature codly.theme(..options) Parameters Parameter Type Default Meaning preset (positional) str or dictionary "thesis" Built-in theme name or a theme dictionary. At most one positional value is accepted. Named options See codly.define-theme None Shared tokens and element dictionaries forwarded to codly.define-theme. The built-in presets are "thesis", "dark", "clean", "github-light", "solarized-light", and "one-light". The "thesis" preset follows Codly's ordinary visual defaults. See codly.themes for the preset dictionaries and codly.define-theme for supported shared tokens, element dictionaries, and merge behavior. Behavior [!TIP] Theme only Codly content. The theme's typography and syntax colors apply inside Codly blocks; ordinary raw text outside them keeps its own styling. Use the returned function as a show rule, commonly #show: codly.theme("dark"). It applies scoped set rules to Codly's block, line, number, language, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, and annotation elements, along with their typography and syntax colors. Named options are passed to codly.define-theme, which validates names and values and combines them with the selected preset. Explicit element fields and later local set rules keep their normal precedence. Example: Basic Usage - type: select name: theme-preset label: Theme default: '"github-light"' options: - label: Thesis value: '"thesis"' - label: Dark value: '"dark"' - label: Clean value: '"clean"' - label: GitHub Light value: '"github-light"' - label: Solarized Light value: '"solarized-light"' - label: One Light value: '"one-light"' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.theme(theme-preset) #codly.new( ```py def double(value): return value * 2 ```, header: [example.py], )

title: themes
text: codly.themes The built-in theme dictionaries, keyed by preset name; use codly.theme to render one or codly.define-theme to derive a reusable configuration. Signature codly.themes: dictionary Its six keys are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. Each value is a theme dictionary. thesis is Codly's default appearance. Preset Appearance thesis Codly's ordinary defaults, with language-colored badges and a light header. dark Dark editor palette with light text and syntax colors. clean Unboxed code with muted text and unpainted language badges. github-light GitHub light editor palette. solarized-light Solarized light editor palette. one-light One Light editor palette. Theme dictionary keys The theme loader accepts these shared token keys and element-section keys. Unknown top-level keys are rejected. Kind Keys Meaning Shared token foreground, muted, fill, accent, stroke, radius, inset Main text, subdued text, code-line fill, accent color, outline, corner radius, and inner spacing. Shared token header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill Fills for headers, footers, and callout bubbles. Shared token syntax, highlight-fill, highlight-colors, language-colors Raw-code syntax theme, highlight fill, highlight color or palette, and whether language badges use their language colors. Element section block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation A dictionary of settings for that Codly element. Fields within a section follow that element's settings; its text field accepts native Typst text settings. The public theme dictionary can be inspected or selected by key. For the exact merge behavior and validation when creating a custom dictionary, see codly.define-theme. Behavior [!TIP] Derive a custom preset. Pass a value such as codly.themes.dark as base to codly.define-theme to start a custom theme from that preset. The preset entries are complete theme dictionaries; looking up a preset does not apply it to the document by itself. Example: Basic Usage Renders one block per preset for side-by-side comparison: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #let source = ```py def double(value): return value * 2 ``` #grid( columns: (1fr, 1fr), gutter: 6pt, ..codly.themes.keys().map(name => { show: codly.theme(name) codly.new(source, header: [#name]) }), )

title: define-theme
text: codly.define-theme Build a reusable theme dictionary by inheriting a built-in preset or another theme, then applying named token and element-setting overrides. Signature codly.define-theme(base: "thesis", ..overrides) base is named and defaults to "thesis"; overrides are named arguments. Positional arguments are not accepted. Parameters Name Type Default Meaning base str or dictionary "thesis" A preset name or an existing theme dictionary. The built-in names are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. foreground paint or auto inherited Text color for code; auto follows the surrounding text. muted paint or auto inherited Muted text color, including line numbers; auto follows the resolved foreground. fill auto, paint or none, array of paints or none, or function inherited Source-line fill. An array cycles by displayed row; a function receives a row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. accent paint inherited Main accent, including the language badge's default color and (unless explicitly overridden) the first highlight color. stroke stroke inherited Default outline for code elements. radius length inherited Default corner radius. inset length or dictionary inherited Default code-line inset. header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill paint or none inherited Backgrounds for the header, footer, and callout bubbles. syntax auto, str, path, or bytes inherited TextMate plist theme for raw-code syntax highlighting. highlight-fill function inherited Callback receiving a highlight color and returning its fill. highlight-colors paint or nonempty array of paints inherited Default highlight color, or a palette cycled by highlights. language-colors bool inherited Whether language badges use their language-specific colors. block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation dictionary inherited Overrides settable fields on the corresponding Codly element. The text entry in a section is a dictionary of native Typst text settings. All defaults are inherited from the selected base. Token names and section names are the complete supported top-level keys. Within a section, use fields supported by the corresponding Codly element. The fill callback's row dictionary uses a zero-based displayed-row index; kind is code, skip, or callout, while source-line and number are none for generated rows or numbers that are not displayed. Behavior [!NOTE] Accent also updates the first highlight color. If you override accent without supplying highlight-colors, the new accent replaces the first inherited highlight color. An explicit palette takes precedence. [!WARNING] Highlight palettes cannot be empty. Passing highlight-colors: () causes a compilation error. The result is a complete dictionary, not a show rule. It starts with the thesis defaults, merges a preset or dictionary base, then merges the named overrides. Section dictionaries merge one level deep, so separate fields such as header: (fill: red) and header: (align: left) can be combined when deriving a theme. Values inside those fields, including callbacks and nested dictionaries, are replaced as complete values. An unknown preset or top-level key raises an error. Every section override must be a dictionary. Pass the returned dictionary to codly.theme to render with it. Theme rules are scoped: explicit element fields and later local set rules can override theme values. Section text settings are applied as text settings to text within that element. Example: Basic Usage - type: select name: accent label: Accent default: 'rgb("ef6c00")' options: - label: Orange value: 'rgb("ef6c00")' - label: Blue value: 'rgb("1565c0")' - label: Green value: 'rgb("2e7d32")' #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #let custom = codly.define-theme( base: "thesis", accent: accent, header: (fill: accent.lighten(80%), align: left), ) #show: codly.theme(custom) #codly.new( ```py return answer ```, header: [Custom theme], highlights: ((line: 1),), )

title: info
text: codly.info Read the source-line count and last displayed line number recorded for a labeled code block. Signature codly.info(target) -> (last-number: int | none, lines: int) Parameters Name Type Default Meaning target label required, positional Label identifying the code block whose metadata to read. The returned dictionary has these fields: Field Type Meaning last-number int or none Last computed displayed line number, or none when the block has no numbered source line. lines int Number of source lines in the block, including lines omitted from its displayed range. Behavior [!WARNING] The target label must identify one code block. Labels resolving to zero or multiple locations, or to a location with no later Codly block record, cause a compilation error. [!NOTE] lines counts the full source. The count includes lines omitted by range; last-number reflects the selected range and offset. Call codly.info inside context, since it queries document content. The helper reads the first Codly block record after the label's location. Unnumbered rows do not replace last-number. Passing the label as another block's offset adds this number to that block's numbering, so numbering can continue across blocks. Example: Basic Usage #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ``` first second ```, )<first-block> #codly.new( ``` third ```, offset: <first-block>, )<continued-block> #context[ First block: #repr(codly.info(<first-block>)) ]

title: ⚙️ Queries and show rules
text: Queries and show rules Use queries to inspect document elements, and show rules to customize how they render. This guide assumes you are comfortable with the component fields. Choose the right tool Codly's components are Elembic custom elements. Use the exported codly.e namespace to inspect fields, filter elements, or read scoped defaults. It provides the same Elembic version Codly uses, without a separate package import. Task Tool Set component defaults #show: codly.number-set_(...) and other *-set_ helpers Wrap or replace a component #show: codly.number-show_(it => ...) and other *-show_ helpers Read an element's resolved fields codly.e.fields(it) Find custom elements in the document codly.e.query(codly.new) inside context Read defaults in the current scope codly.e.get(get => ...) The Codly helpers delegate to codly.e.set_ and codly.e.show_. For example, codly.number-show_(callback) is shorthand for codly.e.show_(codly.number, callback). Native #set codly.number(...) does not configure an Elembic element. Query elements and inspect their fields codly.e.query returns matching custom elements; codly.e.fields returns their field dictionaries. A .with(...) filter compares resolved field values. Use before: here() or after: here() to restrict the query by document location. Elembic's query guide documents these filters and location bounds. #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py print("hello") ```, radius: 8pt, ) #context { let blocks = codly.e.query(codly.new.with(radius: 8pt), before: here()) [Matching blocks: #blocks.len(). Language: #codly.e.fields(blocks.first()).body.lang.] } Use native query(<label>) for labeled content and query(figure) for Typst figures. For custom elements, prefer codly.e.query: codly.selector() and codly.e.selector(codly.number) are native selectors intended for show rules. Their default selectors can match intermediate renderings; they are not reliable instance counters. Elembic's meta: true selector exists for lower-level metadata queries. [!NOTE] Queries inspect the laid-out document They need context and can see content later in the document. Avoid making an element's existence depend on a query that counts that same element: Typst may not converge. For a labeled block's line count, use codly.info. Set defaults, then customize rendering Use *-set_ for fields such as fill, inset, or numbering. A *-show_ callback receives the element, with scoped defaults resolved, and must return content. Use codly.e.fields(it) to read its custom fields; native it.fields() describes Elembic's underlying Typst representation. #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #{ show: codly.number-set_(numbering: "1.") show: codly.e.show_(codly.number.with(number: 2), it => { text(red, weight: "bold", it) }) codly.new( ```py first = 1 second = 2 ```, ) } // The rules above end with their enclosing scope. #codly.new( ```py ordinary = 3 ```, ) Returning it, or wrapping it as above, preserves the component's existing renderer. Returning fresh content replaces that renderer. For example, codly.lang-show_(it => strong(codly.e.fields(it).body)) displays only the language name and bypasses its usual badge rendering. Constructing a new matching component inside its own show rule can trigger the rule again. When you need a native show-set rule, use an Elembic selector: #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show codly.e.selector(codly.header): set text(style: "italic") Read scoped defaults codly.e.get reads settings at its position, even without a component instance. codly.e.fields(it) reads the fields of a particular instance, including explicit constructor arguments. Read resolved fields in show callbacks or query results. A newly constructed instance can still have incomplete fields until Elembic displays it; codly.e.fields(codly.new(...)) is not a way to read all current defaults. #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #show: codly.set_(radius: 8pt) #codly.e.get(get => [Current default radius: #get(codly.new).radius.]) Keep custom rules predictable Put rules before the content they style, and group related rules in a local { ... } scope or template. Target the smallest useful component: a number rule for number formatting, a line rule for rows, a block rule for the whole listing. Prefer existing fields before replacing rendering. Keep callbacks free of document-wide queries when fields already contain the needed information. Codly can create many row and number elements. Preserve it when adding decoration. Replacing rows or whole blocks can remove the syntax, layout, anchors, and metadata produced by their default renderers. Test wrapping, page breaks, and references when a rule changes geometry. Optional diff and syntax features also create internal passes, so an unrestricted query may include supporting elements. For more detail, see Elembic show rules, Typst queries, and Codly internals.

title: ⚙️ Internals
text: How Codly works Codly keeps Typst's syntax highlighting and builds a configurable layout around it. This guide follows the current implementation from source to output, so you can choose the right extension point when a theme or field is not enough. For writing rules and queries, see Querying and show rules. From source to components codly.new is an alias for the block element codly.codly. It accepts raw content, a source string, or a resolved path. Strings and files become block raw elements; filenames can supply a language and file badge. Typst then produces raw.line values containing both plain text and highlighted content. flowchart TD accTitle: From source to a Codly block accDescr: Input becomes highlighted lines, optional syntax passes, displayed rows, components, and grid layout with reference metadata. Input["Raw content, string, or path"] --> Block["codly.new: prepare source and resolve settings"] Block --> Raw["Typst raw: syntax-highlighted raw.line values"] Raw --> Passes["Optional diff, rainbow, and sublanguage passes"] Passes --> Rows["Select source lines and build displayed rows"] Rows --> Parts["Codly components: lines, numbers, badges, highlights, callouts"] Parts --> Grid["Grid layout and optional geometry painting"] Grid --> Output["Rendered block and reference metadata"] The components are Elembic custom elements. Elembic validates fields, casts shorthand configuration values, and resolves scoped set/show rules when elements are displayed. That is why #show: codly.number-set_(...) can style numbers generated later by the block renderer. Themes apply these same scoped rules, alongside raw syntax and text styling. Syntax passes reuse Typst Codly does not implement another language parser. Extra highlighting features create auxiliary raw blocks and retain their highlighted lines: Sublanguages highlight each configured source range with its own language. codly.sublang-block stores those lines as metadata; the visible row receives the resolved raw.line before its line show rule runs. Rainbow delimiters use a private classification theme to distinguish code from strings and comments, then recolor eligible delimiters in the display content. Sublanguage ranges receive their own classification passes. Diffs (diff-py or diff,py, for example) create old and new source views for each hunk. Removed rows use old-side highlighting; added and context rows use new-side highlighting. The final block adds backgrounds and gutters once. These passes can nest: a diff view can contain sublanguages and rainbow colors. Auxiliary blocks provide syntax data rather than extra visible listings. They can still appear in broad element queries, so a count of queried Codly or raw elements need not equal a count of visible listings. Source lines become grid rows The row builder applies ranges, skips, offsets, and unnumbered-line settings. It then inserts callout rows and constructs gutter, code, and optional annotation cells. Annotations can span rows; headers and footers span the columns. Keep three coordinates separate: Coordinate Used for Source line, starting at 1 Ranges, sublanguages, gutter arrays, callout attachment Displayed number Number labels and highlight line selection Displayed row index, starting at 0 Fill palettes and row callbacks, including generated rows Here the second source line displays as 102. Its gutter entry and callout use source coordinates; its highlight uses the displayed number. #import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly #codly.new( ```py x = 1 print(x) ```, offset: 100, gutters: (auto, ("", "→")), highlights: ((line: 102, start: 0, end: 5),), callouts: ((line: 2, body: [The second source line.]),), ) A wrapped line remains one logical code row. Smart indentation formats its continuations inside that row. Body backgrounds normally come from codly.line; whole-line highlights take precedence over diff backgrounds, which take precedence over the ordinary fill. Header and footer components own their fills. Layout, metadata, and references For ordinary blocks, Typst lays out the grid directly. Outside gutters, indent guides, wrap markers, or edge padding use the geometry renderer: metadata marks cell and page-region boundaries, then painting uses their actual positions. This lets decorations follow wrapped rows and page breaks without laying out a second copy of the code. flowchart TD accTitle: Layout and metadata support decorations and references accDescr: The grid supplies geometry marks for painting, hidden targets for references, and a compact block record for info and continued numbering. Grid["Grid and code content"] --> Layout["Typst layout"] Layout --> Bounds["Cell and region metadata"] Bounds --> Paint["Paint fills, borders, guides, and wrap markers"] Grid --> Anchors["Hidden native figure targets"] Anchors --> References["Native references via Codly reference components"] Grid --> Record["Block record: source count and last number"] Record --> Info["codly.info and continued numbering"] Line, highlight, and annotation references use hidden native figure targets, while codly.line-ref and the other reference components format the resulting reference text. The enclosing figure label is discovered automatically; an unlabeled inner figure stops that discovery. codly.info reads the compact block record inside context. Its lines field counts the full source, including omitted lines; last-number tracks computed numbering. Passing a previous block's label as offset uses that record to continue numbering. Finding an extension point Start with public fields and themes for layout and appearance. Use component show rules for a badge, line, highlight, or reference; keep the original element in your result when you want its existing behavior. Query metadata for document inspection after layout. For implementation work, field types, defaults, and descriptions live in src/args.yaml. src/declarations.typ loads this metadata for the constructors, casts, and renderers in codly.typ. The row and block pipeline lives in src/lib.typ, and the position-based painting in src/geometry.typ. Fields and labels beginning with __ carry internal data and may change; build customizations on the documented API.
